  259|       |//! UTF-16 encoding.
  260|       |/*! http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-16
  261|       |    http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2781
  262|       |    \tparam CharType Type for storing 16-bit UTF-16 data. Default is wchar_t. C++11 may use char16_t instead.
  263|       |    \note implements Encoding concept
  264|       |
  265|       |    \note For in-memory access, no need to concern endianness. The code units and code points are represented by CPU's endianness.
  266|       |    For streaming, use UTF16LE and UTF16BE, which handle endianness.
  267|       |*/
  268|       |template<typename CharType = wchar_t>
  269|       |struct UTF16 {
  270|       |    typedef CharType Ch;
  271|       |    CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(Ch) >= 2);
  272|       |
  273|       |    enum { supportUnicode = 1 };
  274|       |
  275|       |    template<typename OutputStream>
  276|       |    static void Encode(OutputStream& os, unsigned codepoint) {
  277|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename OutputStream::Ch) >= 2);
  278|       |        if (codepoint <= 0xFFFF) {
  279|       |            CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(codepoint < 0xD800 || codepoint > 0xDFFF); // Code point itself cannot be surrogate pair
  280|       |            os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>(codepoint));
  281|       |        }
  282|       |        else {
  283|       |            CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(codepoint <= 0x10FFFF);
  284|       |            unsigned v = codepoint - 0x10000;
  285|       |            os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>((v >> 10) | 0xD800));
  286|       |            os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>((v & 0x3FF) | 0xDC00));
  287|       |        }
  288|       |    }
  289|       |
  290|       |
  291|       |    template<typename OutputStream>
  292|       |    static void EncodeUnsafe(OutputStream& os, unsigned codepoint) {
  293|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename OutputStream::Ch) >= 2);
  294|       |        if (codepoint <= 0xFFFF) {
  295|       |            CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(codepoint < 0xD800 || codepoint > 0xDFFF); // Code point itself cannot be surrogate pair
  296|       |            PutUnsafe(os, static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>(codepoint));
  297|       |        }
  298|       |        else {
  299|       |            CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_ASSERT(codepoint <= 0x10FFFF);
  300|       |            unsigned v = codepoint - 0x10000;
  301|       |            PutUnsafe(os, static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>((v >> 10) | 0xD800));
  302|       |            PutUnsafe(os, static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>((v & 0x3FF) | 0xDC00));
  303|       |        }
  304|       |    }
  305|       |
  306|       |    template <typename InputStream>
  307|       |    static bool Decode(InputStream& is, unsigned* codepoint) {
  308|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename InputStream::Ch) >= 2);
  309|       |        typename InputStream::Ch c = is.Take();
  310|       |        if (c < 0xD800 || c > 0xDFFF) {
  311|       |            *codepoint = static_cast<unsigned>(c);
  312|       |            return true;
  313|       |        }
  314|       |        else if (c <= 0xDBFF) {
  315|       |            *codepoint = (static_cast<unsigned>(c) & 0x3FF) << 10;
  316|       |            c = is.Take();
  317|       |            *codepoint |= (static_cast<unsigned>(c) & 0x3FF);
  318|       |            *codepoint += 0x10000;
  319|       |            return c >= 0xDC00 && c <= 0xDFFF;
  320|       |        }
  321|       |        return false;
  322|       |    }
  323|       |
  324|       |    template <typename InputStream, typename OutputStream>
  325|       |    static bool Validate(InputStream& is, OutputStream& os) {
  326|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename InputStream::Ch) >= 2);
  327|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename OutputStream::Ch) >= 2);
  328|       |        typename InputStream::Ch c;
  329|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputStream::Ch>(c = is.Take()));
  330|       |        if (c < 0xD800 || c > 0xDFFF)
  331|       |            return true;
  332|       |        else if (c <= 0xDBFF) {
  333|       |            os.Put(c = is.Take());
  334|       |            return c >= 0xDC00 && c <= 0xDFFF;
  335|       |        }
  336|       |        return false;
  337|       |    }
  338|       |};
  339|       |
  340|       |//! UTF-16 little endian encoding.
  341|       |template<typename CharType = wchar_t>
  342|       |struct UTF16LE : UTF16<CharType> {
  343|       |    template <typename InputByteStream>
  344|       |    static CharType TakeBOM(InputByteStream& is) {
  345|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename InputByteStream::Ch) == 1);
  346|       |        CharType c = Take(is);
  347|       |        return static_cast<uint16_t>(c) == 0xFEFFu ? Take(is) : c;
  348|       |    }
  349|       |
  350|       |    template <typename InputByteStream>
  351|       |    static CharType Take(InputByteStream& is) {
  352|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename InputByteStream::Ch) == 1);
  353|       |        unsigned c = static_cast<uint8_t>(is.Take());
  354|       |        c |= static_cast<unsigned>(static_cast<uint8_t>(is.Take())) << 8;
  355|       |        return static_cast<CharType>(c);
  356|       |    }
  357|       |
  358|       |    template <typename OutputByteStream>
  359|       |    static void PutBOM(OutputByteStream& os) {
  360|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename OutputByteStream::Ch) == 1);
  361|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>(0xFFu));
  362|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>(0xFEu));
  363|       |    }
  364|       |
  365|       |    template <typename OutputByteStream>
  366|       |    static void Put(OutputByteStream& os, CharType c) {
  367|       |        CEREAL_RAPIDJSON_STATIC_ASSERT(sizeof(typename OutputByteStream::Ch) == 1);
  368|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>(static_cast<unsigned>(c) & 0xFFu));
  369|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>((static_cast<unsigned>(c) >> 8) & 0xFFu));
  370|       |    }
  371|       |};

  456|       |template<typename CharType = unsigned>
  457|       |struct UTF32LE : UTF32<CharType> {

  480|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>(0x00u));
  481|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>(0x00u));
  482|       |    }

  488|       |        os.Put(static_cast<typename OutputByteStream::Ch>((c >> 8) & 0xFFu));

  491|       |    }

  293|       |        else
  294|       |            return p;

    1|       |/**
    2|       | *  @note This file is part of Empirical, https://github.com/devosoft/Empirical
    3|       | *  @copyright Copyright (C) Michigan State University, MIT Software license; see doc/LICENSE.md
    4|       | *  @date 2016-2020.
    5|       | *
    6|       | *  @file Ptr.hpp
    7|       | *  @brief A wrapper for pointers that does careful memory tracking (but only in debug mode).
    8|       | *  @note Status: BETA
    9|       | *
   10|       | *  Ptr objects behave as normal pointers under most conditions.  However, if a program is
   11|       | *  compiled with EMP_TRACK_MEM set, then these pointers perform extra tests to ensure that
   12|       | *  they point to valid memory and that memory is freed before pointers are released.
   13|       | *
   14|       | *  If you trip an assert, you can re-do the run a track a specific pointer by defining
   15|       | *  EMP_ABORT_PTR_NEW or EMP_ABORT_PTR_DELETE to the ID of the pointer in question.  This will
   16|       | *  allow you to track the pointer more easily in a debugger.
   17|       | *
   18|       | *  @todo Track information about emp::vector and emp::array objects to make sure we don't
   19|       | *    point directly into them? (A resize() could make such pointers invalid!) Or better, warn
   20|       | *    it vector memory could have moved.
   21|       | *  @todo Get working with threads
   22|       | */
   23|       |
   24|       |#ifndef EMP_PTR_H

   11|       | *       gives access to bit fields for easy access to different sized chucnk of bits and
   12|       | *       implementation new bit-magic tricks.
   13|       | */

   36|       |  /// SFINAE helper to determine field_t for BitSet
   37|       |  template <size_t NUM_BITS> struct FieldHelper {
   38|       |#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
   39|       |    ///< Field sizes are 32 bits in Emscripten (max directly handled)
   40|       |    using field_t = uint32_t;
   41|       |#else
   42|       |    ///< Field sizes are 64 bits in native, unless NUM_BITS == 32
   43|       |    using field_t = uint64_t;
   44|       |#endif
   45|       |  };
   46|       |
   47|       |  template <> struct FieldHelper<32> {
   48|       |    // if NUM_BITS == 32, use uint32_t
   49|       |    using field_t = uint32_t;
   50|       |  };
   51|       |
   52|       |  ///  A fixed-sized (but arbitrarily large) array of bits, and optimizes operations on those bits
   53|       |  ///  to be as fast as possible.
   54|       |  template <size_t NUM_BITS> class BitSet {
   55|       |
   56|       |  // make all templated instantiations friends with each other
   57|       |  template<size_t FRIEND_BITS> friend class BitSet;
   58|       |
   59|       |  private:
   60|       |
   61|       |    ///< field size is 64 for native (except NUM_BITS == 32), 32 for emscripten
   62|       |    using field_t = typename FieldHelper<NUM_BITS>::field_t;
   63|       |
   64|       |    ///< How many bytes are in a field?
   65|       |    static constexpr field_t FIELD_BYTES = sizeof(field_t);
   66|       |
   67|       |    ///< How many bits are in a field?
   68|       |    static constexpr field_t FIELD_BITS = 8 * FIELD_BYTES;
   69|       |
   70|       |    static constexpr field_t FIELD_LOG2 = emp::Log2(FIELD_BITS);
   71|       |
   72|       |    /// Fields hold bits in groups of 32 or 64 (as uint32_t or uint64_t);
   73|       |    /// how many fields do we need?
   74|       |    static constexpr field_t NUM_FIELDS = (1 + ((NUM_BITS - 1) / FIELD_BITS));
   75|       |
   76|       |    /// End position of the stored bits in the last field; 0 if perfect fit.
   77|       |    static constexpr field_t LAST_BIT = NUM_BITS & (FIELD_BITS - 1);
   78|       |
   79|       |    /// How many total bytes are needed to represent these bits? (rounded up to full bytes)
   80|       |    static const field_t NUM_BYTES = 1 + ((NUM_BITS - 1) >> 3);
   81|       |
   82|       |    field_t bit_set[NUM_FIELDS];  ///< Fields to hold the actual bits for this BitSet.
   83|       |
   84|       |    /// BitProxy lets us use operator[] on with BitSet as an lvalue.
   85|       |    class BitProxy {
   86|       |    private:
   87|       |      BitSet<NUM_BITS> & bit_set;  ///< BitSet object that this proxy refers to.
   88|       |      size_t index;                ///< Position in BitSet the this proxy refers to.
   89|       |    public:
   90|       |      BitProxy(BitSet<NUM_BITS> & _set, size_t _idx) : bit_set(_set), index(_idx) {
   91|       |        emp_assert(_idx < bit_set.size());
   92|       |      }
   93|       |
   94|       |      /// Set the bit value that this proxy refers to.
   95|       |      BitProxy & operator=(bool b) {    // lvalue handling...
   96|       |        bit_set.Set(index, b);
   97|       |        return *this;
   98|       |      }
   99|       |
  100|       |      /// Convert BitProxy to a regular boolean value.
  101|       |      operator bool() const {            // rvalue handling...
  102|       |        return bit_set.Get(index);
  103|       |      }
  104|       |
  105|       |      /// Flip this bit.
  106|       |      BitProxy & Toggle() { bit_set.Toggle(index); return *this; }
  107|       |    };
  108|       |    friend class BitProxy;
  109|       |
  110|      9|    inline static size_t FieldID(const size_t index) {
  111|      9|      emp_assert((index >> FIELD_LOG2) < NUM_FIELDS);
  112|      0|      return index >> FIELD_LOG2;
  113|      9|    }
  114|       |
  115|      9|    inline static size_t FieldPos(const size_t index) {
  116|      9|      return index & (FIELD_BITS - 1);
  117|      9|    }
  118|       |
  119|       |    inline static size_t Byte2Field(const size_t index) {
  120|       |      return index / FIELD_BYTES;
  121|       |    }
  122|       |
  123|       |    inline static size_t Byte2FieldPos(const size_t index) {
  124|       |      return FieldPos(index * 8);
  125|       |    }
  126|       |
  127|     43|    inline void Copy(const field_t in_set[NUM_FIELDS]) {
  128|     43|      std::memcpy(bit_set, in_set, sizeof(bit_set));
  129|     43|    }
  130|       |
  131|       |    template<size_t shift>
  132|      0|    void ShiftLeft() {
  133|       |      // profiled this templated, special case variant
  134|       |      // and did see a difference in runtime MAM
  135|       |
  136|       |      // TODO currently only implemented for NUM_FIELDS == 1
  137|       |      //static_assert( NUM_FIELDS == 1 );
  138|       |      //static_assert( LAST_BIT == 0 );
  139|       |      if constexpr (NUM_FIELDS != 1) {
  140|       |        ShiftLeft(shift);
  141|       |
  142|       |      }
  143|      0|      else {
  144|       |        if constexpr (LAST_BIT != 0)
  145|       |            bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
  146|      0|        bit_set[0] <<= shift;
  147|      0|      }
  148|      0|    }
  149|       |
  150|       |    /// Helper: call SHIFT with positive number instead
  151|       |    void ShiftLeft(const size_t shift_size) {
  152|       |
  153|       |      if (shift_size > NUM_BITS) {
  154|       |        Clear();
  155|       |        return;
  156|       |      }
  157|       |
  158|       |      const int field_shift = shift_size / FIELD_BITS;
  159|       |      const int bit_shift = shift_size % FIELD_BITS;
  160|       |      const int bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
  161|       |
  162|       |      // Loop through each field, from L to R, and update it.
  163|       |      if (field_shift) {
  164|       |        for (int i = NUM_FIELDS - 1; i >= field_shift; --i) {
  165|       |          bit_set[i] = bit_set[i - field_shift];
  166|       |        }
  167|       |        for (int i = field_shift - 1; i >= 0; i--) bit_set[i] = 0;
  168|       |      }
  169|       |
  170|       |      // account for bit_shift
  171|       |      if (bit_shift) {
  172|       |        for (int i = NUM_FIELDS - 1; i > field_shift; --i) {
  173|       |          bit_set[i] <<= bit_shift;
  174|       |          bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i-1] >> bit_overflow);
  175|       |        }
  176|       |        // Handle final field (field_shift position)
  177|       |        bit_set[field_shift] <<= bit_shift;
  178|       |      }
  179|       |
  180|       |      // Mask out any bits that have left-shifted away
  181|       |      if (LAST_BIT) { bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT); }
  182|       |    }
  183|       |
  184|       |
  185|       |    /// Helper for calling SHIFT with negative number
  186|       |    void ShiftRight(const size_t shift_size) {
  187|       |      if (!shift_size) return;
  188|       |
  189|       |      const field_t field_shift = shift_size / FIELD_BITS;
  190|       |
  191|       |      // only clear and return if we are field_shift-ing
  192|       |      // we want to be able to always shift by up to a byte
  193|       |      // so that Import and Export work
  194|       |      if (field_shift && shift_size > NUM_BITS) {
  195|       |        Clear();
  196|       |        return;
  197|       |      }
  198|       |      const field_t bit_shift = shift_size % FIELD_BITS;
  199|       |      const field_t bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
  200|       |
  201|       |      // account for field_shift
  202|       |      if (field_shift) {
  203|       |        for (size_t i = 0; i < (NUM_FIELDS - field_shift); ++i) {
  204|       |          bit_set[i] = bit_set[i + field_shift];
  205|       |        }
  206|       |        for (size_t i = NUM_FIELDS - field_shift; i < NUM_FIELDS; i++) bit_set[i] = 0;
  207|       |      }
  208|       |
  209|       |      // account for bit_shift
  210|       |      if (bit_shift) {
  211|       |        for (size_t i = 0; i < (NUM_FIELDS - 1 - field_shift); ++i) {
  212|       |          bit_set[i] >>= bit_shift;
  213|       |          bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i+1] << bit_overflow);
  214|       |        }
  215|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1 - field_shift] >>= bit_shift;
  216|       |      }
  217|       |    }
  218|       |
  219|       |    /// Helper: call ROTATE with negative number instead
  220|       |    void RotateLeft(const size_t shift_size_raw) {
  221|       |      const field_t shift_size = shift_size_raw % NUM_BITS;
  222|       |
  223|       |      // use different approaches based on BitSet size
  224|       |      if constexpr (NUM_FIELDS == 1) {
  225|       |        // special case: for exactly one field_T, try to go low level
  226|       |        // adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/776508/best-practices-for-circular-shift-rotate-operations-in-c
  227|       |        field_t & n = bit_set[0];
  228|       |        field_t c = shift_size;
  229|       |
  230|       |        // mask necessary to suprress shift count overflow warnings
  231|       |        constexpr field_t mask = MaskLow<field_t>(FIELD_LOG2);
  232|       |
  233|       |        c &= mask;
  234|       |        n = (n<<c) | (n>>( (-(c+FIELD_BITS-NUM_BITS))&mask ));
  235|       |
  236|       |      } else if (NUM_FIELDS < 32) {
  237|       |        // for small BitSets, shifting L/R and ORing is faster
  238|       |        emp::BitSet<NUM_BITS> dup(*this);
  239|       |        dup.ShiftLeft(shift_size);
  240|       |        ShiftRight(NUM_BITS - shift_size);
  241|       |        OR_SELF(dup);
  242|       |      } else {
  243|       |        // for big BitSets, manual rotating is fater
  244|       |
  245|       |        // note that we already modded shift_size by NUM_BITS
  246|       |        // so there's no need to mod by FIELD_SIZE here
  247|       |        const int field_shift = LAST_BIT ? (
  248|       |          (shift_size + FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT) / FIELD_BITS
  249|       |        ) : (
  250|       |          shift_size / FIELD_BITS
  251|       |        );
  252|       |        // if we field shift, we need to shift bits by (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT)
  253|       |        // more to account for the filler that gets pulled out of the middle
  254|       |        const int bit_shift = LAST_BIT && field_shift ? (
  255|       |          (shift_size + FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT) % FIELD_BITS
  256|       |        ) : (
  257|       |          shift_size % FIELD_BITS
  258|       |        );
  259|       |        const int bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
  260|       |
  261|       |        // if rotating more than field capacity, we need to rotate fields
  262|       |        std::rotate(
  263|       |          std::rbegin(bit_set),
  264|       |          std::rbegin(bit_set)+field_shift,
  265|       |          std::rend(bit_set)
  266|       |        );
  267|       |
  268|       |        // if necessary, shift filler bits out of the middle
  269|       |        if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
  270|       |          const int filler_idx = (NUM_FIELDS - 1 + field_shift) % NUM_FIELDS;
  271|       |          for (int i = filler_idx + 1; i < (int)NUM_FIELDS; ++i) {
  272|       |            bit_set[i-1] |= bit_set[i] << LAST_BIT;
  273|       |            bit_set[i] >>= (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT);
  274|       |          }
  275|       |        }
  276|       |
  277|       |        // account for bit_shift
  278|       |        if (bit_shift) {
  279|       |
  280|       |          const field_t keystone = LAST_BIT ? (
  281|       |            (bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] << (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT))
  282|       |            | (bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 2] >> LAST_BIT)
  283|       |          ) : (
  284|       |            bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1]
  285|       |          );
  286|       |
  287|       |          for (int i = NUM_FIELDS - 1; i > 0; --i) {
  288|       |            bit_set[i] <<= bit_shift;
  289|       |            bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i-1] >> bit_overflow);
  290|       |          }
  291|       |          // Handle final field
  292|       |          bit_set[0] <<= bit_shift;
  293|       |          bit_set[0] |= keystone >> bit_overflow;
  294|       |
  295|       |        }
  296|       |
  297|       |      }
  298|       |
  299|       |      // Mask out filler bits
  300|       |      if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
  301|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
  302|       |      }
  303|       |
  304|       |    }
  305|       |
  306|       |
  307|       |    /// Helper for calling ROTATE with positive number
  308|       |    void RotateRight(const size_t shift_size_raw) {
  309|       |
  310|       |      const field_t shift_size = shift_size_raw % NUM_BITS;
  311|       |
  312|       |      // use different approaches based on BitSet size
  313|       |      if constexpr (NUM_FIELDS == 1) {
  314|       |        // special case: for exactly one field_t, try to go low level
  315|       |        // adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/776508/best-practices-for-circular-shift-rotate-operations-in-c
  316|       |
  317|       |        field_t & n = bit_set[0];
  318|       |        field_t c = shift_size;
  319|       |
  320|       |        // mask necessary to suprress shift count overflow warnings
  321|       |        constexpr field_t mask = MaskLow<field_t>(FIELD_LOG2);
  322|       |
  323|       |        c &= mask;
  324|       |        n = (n>>c) | (n<<( (NUM_BITS-c)&mask ));
  325|       |
  326|       |      } else if (NUM_FIELDS < 32) {
  327|       |        // for small BitSets, shifting L/R and ORing is faster
  328|       |        emp::BitSet<NUM_BITS> dup(*this);
  329|       |        dup.ShiftRight(shift_size);
  330|       |        ShiftLeft(NUM_BITS - shift_size);
  331|       |        OR_SELF(dup);
  332|       |      } else {
  333|       |        // for big BitSets, manual rotating is fater
  334|       |
  335|       |        const field_t field_shift = (shift_size / FIELD_BITS) % NUM_FIELDS;
  336|       |        const int bit_shift = shift_size % FIELD_BITS;
  337|       |        const field_t bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
  338|       |
  339|       |        // if rotating more than field capacity, we need to rotate fields
  340|       |        std::rotate(
  341|       |          std::begin(bit_set),
  342|       |          std::begin(bit_set)+field_shift,
  343|       |          std::end(bit_set)
  344|       |        );
  345|       |
  346|       |        // if necessary, shift filler bits out of the middle
  347|       |        if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
  348|       |          const int filler_idx = NUM_FIELDS - 1 - field_shift;
  349|       |          for (int i = filler_idx + 1; i < (int)NUM_FIELDS; ++i) {
  350|       |            bit_set[i-1] |= bit_set[i] << LAST_BIT;
  351|       |            bit_set[i] >>= (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT);
  352|       |          }
  353|       |        }
  354|       |
  355|       |        // account for bit_shift
  356|       |        if (bit_shift) {
  357|       |
  358|       |          const field_t keystone = LAST_BIT ? (
  359|       |            bit_set[0] >> (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT)
  360|       |          ) : (
  361|       |            bit_set[0]
  362|       |          );
  363|       |
  364|       |          if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
  365|       |            bit_set[NUM_FIELDS-1] |= bit_set[0] << LAST_BIT;
  366|       |          }
  367|       |
  368|       |          for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_FIELDS - 1; ++i) {
  369|       |            bit_set[i] >>= bit_shift;
  370|       |            bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i+1] << bit_overflow);
  371|       |          }
  372|       |          bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] >>= bit_shift;
  373|       |          bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] |= keystone << bit_overflow;
  374|       |        }
  375|       |      }
  376|       |
  377|       |      // Mask out filler bits
  378|       |      if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
  379|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
  380|       |      }
  381|       |
  382|       |    }

  397|       |    /// Constructor to generate a BitSet from a std::bitset.
  398|       |    explicit BitSet(const std::bitset<NUM_BITS>& bitset) {
  399|       |      Clear(); // have to clear out field bits beyond NUM_BITS
  400|       |      for (size_t bit{}; bit < NUM_BITS; ++bit) Set( bit, bitset[bit] );
  401|       |    }

  411|       |      // TODO: should we enforce the initializer list to be the same length as the bitset?
  412|       |      // emp_assert(l.size() == NUM_BITS);
  413|       |

  416|       |
  417|       |      Clear();
  418|       |

  420|       |      for (auto i = std::rbegin(l); i != std::rend(l); ++i) {
  421|       |        Set(idx, *i);
  422|       |        ++idx;
  423|       |      }
  424|       |
  425|       |    }

  436|       |    /// Set all bits randomly, with a 50% probability of being a 0 or 1.
  437|      0|    void Randomize(Random & random) {
  438|       |      // Randomize all fields, then mask off bits in the last field if not complete.
  439|       |
  440|      0|      random.RandFill(
  441|      0|        reinterpret_cast<unsigned char*>(bit_set),
  442|      0|        (NUM_BITS+7)/8
  443|      0|      );
  444|       |
  445|       |      if constexpr (static_cast<bool>(LAST_BIT)) {
  446|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS-1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(NUM_BITS%32);
  447|       |      }
  448|       |
  449|      0|    }

  451|       |    /// Set all bits randomly, with a given probability of being a 1.
  452|       |    void Randomize(Random & random, const double p1) {
  453|       |      if (p1 == 0.5) return Randomize(random); // If 0.5 probability, generate by field!
  454|       |      for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_BITS; i++) Set(i, random.P(p1));
  455|       |    }
  456|       |
  457|       |  /// Mutate bits, return how many mutations were performed
  458|       |  size_t Mutate(
  459|       |    Random & random,
  460|       |    const size_t num_muts, // @CAO: use tools/Binomial in Distribution.h with this part?
  461|       |    const size_t min_idx=0 // draw this from a distribution to make some
  462|       |                           // bits more volatile than others
  463|       |  ) {
  464|       |    emp_assert(min_idx <= NUM_BITS);
  465|       |    emp_assert(num_muts <= NUM_BITS - min_idx);
  466|       |
  467|       |    std::vector<size_t> res;
  468|       |    Choose(random, NUM_BITS - min_idx, num_muts, res);
  469|       |
  470|       |    for (size_t idx : res) Toggle(idx + min_idx);
  471|       |
  472|       |    return num_muts;
  473|       |
  474|       |  }

  476|       |    /// Assign from a BitSet of a different size.
  477|       |    template <size_t FROM_BITS>
  478|       |    BitSet & Import(
  479|       |      const BitSet<FROM_BITS> & from_set,
  480|       |      const size_t from_bit=0
  481|       |    ) {
  482|       |
  483|       |      if constexpr (FROM_BITS == NUM_BITS) emp_assert(&from_set != this);
  484|       |
  485|       |      emp_assert(from_bit < FROM_BITS);
  486|       |
  487|       |      if (FROM_BITS - from_bit < NUM_BITS) Clear();
  488|       |
  489|       |      const size_t DEST_BYTES = (NUM_BITS + 7)/8;
  490|       |      const size_t FROM_BYTES = (FROM_BITS + 7)/8 - from_bit/8;
  491|       |
  492|       |      const size_t COPY_BYTES = std::min(DEST_BYTES, FROM_BYTES);
  493|       |
  494|       |      std::memcpy(
  495|       |        bit_set,
  496|       |        reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(from_set.bit_set) + from_bit/8,
  497|       |        COPY_BYTES
  498|       |      );
  499|       |
  500|       |      if (from_bit%8) {
  501|       |
  502|       |        this->ShiftRight(from_bit%8);

  505|       |          reinterpret_cast<unsigned char*>(bit_set)[COPY_BYTES-1] |= (
  506|       |            reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(

  511|       |        }
  512|       |
  513|       |      }
  514|       |
  515|       |      // mask out filler bits
  516|       |      if constexpr (static_cast<bool>(LAST_BIT)) {
  517|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
  518|       |      }

  520|       |      return *this;
  521|       |
  522|       |    }

  857|       |    /// Count 1's by looping through once for each bit equal to 1
  858|       |    size_t CountOnes_Sparse() const {
  859|       |      size_t bit_count = 0;
  860|       |      for (auto i : bit_set) {
  861|       |        while (i) {
  862|       |          i &= (i-1);       // Peel off a single 1.
  863|       |          bit_count++;      // And increment the counter
  864|       |        }
  865|       |      }
  866|       |      return bit_count;
  867|       |    }

  869|       |    /// Count 1's in semi-parallel; fastest for even 0's & 1's
  870|       |    size_t CountOnes_Mixed() const {
  871|       |
  872|       |      size_t bit_count = 0;
  873|       |      for (size_t f = 0; f < NUM_FIELDS; ++f) {
  874|       |          // when compiling with -O3 and -msse4.2, this is the fastest population count method.
  875|       |          // this is due to using a dedicated instuction that runs in 1 clock cycle.
  876|       |          std::bitset<FIELD_BITS> std_bs(bit_set[f]);
  877|       |          bit_count += std_bs.count();
  878|       |       }
  879|       |
  880|       |      return bit_count;
  881|       |    }

  887|       |    int FindBit() const {

  889|       |      while (field_id < NUM_FIELDS && bit_set[field_id]==0) field_id++;
  890|       |      return (field_id < NUM_FIELDS) ? (int) (find_bit(bit_set[field_id]) + (field_id << FIELD_LOG2)) : -1;
  891|       |    }

  893|       |    /// Return index of first one in sequence (or -1 if no ones); change this position to zero.
  894|       |    int PopBit() {
  895|       |      size_t field_id = 0;
  896|       |      while (field_id < NUM_FIELDS && bit_set[field_id]==0) field_id++;
  897|       |      if (field_id == NUM_FIELDS) return -1;  // Failed to find bit!
  898|       |
  899|       |      const int pos_found = (int) find_bit(bit_set[field_id]);
  900|       |      bit_set[field_id] &= ~(1U << pos_found);
  901|       |      return pos_found + (int)(field_id << FIELD_LOG2);
  902|       |    }

 1073|       |    BitSet & REVERSE_SELF() {

 1075|       |      // reverse bytes
 1076|       |      std::reverse(
 1077|       |        reinterpret_cast<unsigned char *>(bit_set),
 1078|       |        reinterpret_cast<unsigned char *>(bit_set) + NUM_BYTES
 1079|       |      );
 1080|       |
 1081|       |      // reverse each byte
 1082|       |      // adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2602823/in-c-c-whats-the-simplest-way-to-reverse-the-order-of-bits-in-a-byte
 1083|       |      for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_BYTES; ++i) {
 1084|       |        unsigned char & b = reinterpret_cast<unsigned char *>(bit_set)[i];
 1085|       |        b = (b & 0xF0) >> 4 | (b & 0x0F) << 4;
 1086|       |        b = (b & 0xCC) >> 2 | (b & 0x33) << 2;
 1087|       |        b = (b & 0xAA) >> 1 | (b & 0x55) << 1;
 1088|       |      }

 1091|       |      if constexpr (static_cast<bool>((8-NUM_BITS%8)%8)) {
 1092|       |        this->ShiftRight((8-NUM_BITS%8)%8);
 1093|       |      }

 1097|       |    }

 1123|       |    /// Helper: call ROTATE with negative number instead
 1124|       |    template<size_t shift_size_raw>
 1125|       |    BitSet & ROTL_SELF() {
 1126|       |      constexpr field_t shift_size = shift_size_raw % NUM_BITS;
 1127|       |
 1128|       |      // special case: for exactly one field_t, try to go low level
 1129|       |      // adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/776508/best-practices-for-circular-shift-rotate-operations-in-c
 1130|       |      if constexpr (NUM_FIELDS == 1) {
 1131|       |        field_t & n = bit_set[0];
 1132|       |        field_t c = shift_size;
 1133|       |
 1134|       |        // mask necessary to suprress shift count overflow warnings
 1135|       |        constexpr field_t mask = MaskLow<field_t>(FIELD_LOG2);
 1136|       |
 1137|       |        c &= mask;
 1138|       |        n = (n<<c) | (n>>( (-(c+FIELD_BITS-NUM_BITS))&mask ));
 1139|       |
 1140|       |      } else {
 1141|       |
 1142|       |        // note that we already modded shift_size by NUM_BITS
 1143|       |        // so there's no need to mod by FIELD_SIZE here
 1144|       |        constexpr int field_shift = LAST_BIT ? (
 1145|       |          (shift_size + FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT) / FIELD_BITS
 1146|       |        ) : (
 1147|       |          shift_size / FIELD_BITS
 1148|       |        );
 1149|       |        // if we field shift, we need to shift bits by (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT)
 1150|       |        // more to account for the filler that gets pulled out of the middle
 1151|       |        constexpr int bit_shift = LAST_BIT && field_shift ? (
 1152|       |          (shift_size + FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT) % FIELD_BITS
 1153|       |        ) : (
 1154|       |          shift_size % FIELD_BITS
 1155|       |        );
 1156|       |        constexpr int bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
 1157|       |
 1158|       |        // if rotating more than field capacity, we need to rotate fields
 1159|       |        if constexpr ((bool)field_shift) {
 1160|       |          std::rotate(
 1161|       |            std::rbegin(bit_set),
 1162|       |            std::rbegin(bit_set)+field_shift,
 1163|       |            std::rend(bit_set)
 1164|       |          );
 1165|       |        }
 1166|       |
 1167|       |        // if necessary, shift filler bits out of the middle
 1168|       |        if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
 1169|       |          const int filler_idx = (NUM_FIELDS - 1 + field_shift) % NUM_FIELDS;
 1170|       |          for (int i = filler_idx + 1; i < (int)NUM_FIELDS; ++i) {
 1171|       |            bit_set[i-1] |= bit_set[i] << LAST_BIT;
 1172|       |            bit_set[i] >>= (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT);
 1173|       |          }
 1174|       |        }
 1175|       |
 1176|       |        // account for bit_shift
 1177|       |        if (bit_shift) {
 1178|       |
 1179|       |          const field_t keystone = LAST_BIT ? (
 1180|       |            (bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] << (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT))
 1181|       |            | (bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 2] >> LAST_BIT)
 1182|       |          ) : (
 1183|       |            bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1]
 1184|       |          );
 1185|       |
 1186|       |          for (int i = NUM_FIELDS - 1; i > 0; --i) {
 1187|       |            bit_set[i] <<= bit_shift;
 1188|       |            bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i-1] >> bit_overflow);
 1189|       |          }
 1190|       |          // Handle final field
 1191|       |          bit_set[0] <<= bit_shift;
 1192|       |          bit_set[0] |= keystone >> bit_overflow;
 1193|       |
 1194|       |        }
 1195|       |
 1196|       |      }
 1197|       |
 1198|       |      // mask out filler bits
 1199|       |      if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
 1200|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
 1201|       |      }
 1202|       |
 1203|       |      return *this;
 1204|       |
 1205|       |    }

 1208|       |    /// Helper for calling ROTATE with positive number
 1209|       |    template<size_t shift_size_raw>
 1210|       |    BitSet & ROTR_SELF() {
 1211|       |
 1212|       |      constexpr field_t shift_size = shift_size_raw % NUM_BITS;
 1213|       |
 1214|       |      // special case: for exactly one field_t, try to go low level
 1215|       |      // adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/776508/best-practices-for-circular-shift-rotate-operations-in-c
 1216|       |      if constexpr (NUM_FIELDS == 1) {
 1217|       |        field_t & n = bit_set[0];
 1218|       |        field_t c = shift_size;
 1219|       |
 1220|       |        // mask necessary to suprress shift count overflow warnings
 1221|       |        constexpr field_t mask = MaskLow<field_t>(FIELD_LOG2);
 1222|       |
 1223|       |        c &= mask;
 1224|       |        n = (n>>c) | (n<<( (NUM_BITS-c)&mask ));
 1225|       |
 1226|       |      } else {
 1227|       |
 1228|       |        constexpr field_t field_shift = (shift_size / FIELD_BITS) % NUM_FIELDS;
 1229|       |        constexpr int bit_shift = shift_size % FIELD_BITS;
 1230|       |        constexpr field_t bit_overflow = FIELD_BITS - bit_shift;
 1231|       |
 1232|       |        // if rotating more than field capacity, we need to rotate fields
 1233|       |        if constexpr ((bool)field_shift) {
 1234|       |          std::rotate(
 1235|       |            std::begin(bit_set),
 1236|       |            std::begin(bit_set)+field_shift,
 1237|       |            std::end(bit_set)
 1238|       |          );
 1239|       |        }
 1240|       |
 1241|       |        // if necessary, shift filler bits out of the middle
 1242|       |        if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
 1243|       |          constexpr int filler_idx = NUM_FIELDS - 1 - field_shift;
 1244|       |          for (int i = filler_idx + 1; i < (int)NUM_FIELDS; ++i) {
 1245|       |            bit_set[i-1] |= bit_set[i] << LAST_BIT;
 1246|       |            bit_set[i] >>= (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT);
 1247|       |          }
 1248|       |        }
 1249|       |
 1250|       |        // account for bit_shift
 1251|       |        if (bit_shift) {
 1252|       |
 1253|       |          const field_t keystone = LAST_BIT ? (
 1254|       |            bit_set[0] >> (FIELD_BITS - LAST_BIT)
 1255|       |          ) : (
 1256|       |            bit_set[0]
 1257|       |          );
 1258|       |
 1259|       |          if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
 1260|       |            bit_set[NUM_FIELDS-1] |= bit_set[0] << LAST_BIT;
 1261|       |          }
 1262|       |
 1263|       |          for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_FIELDS - 1; ++i) {
 1264|       |            bit_set[i] >>= bit_shift;
 1265|       |            bit_set[i] |= (bit_set[i+1] << bit_overflow);
 1266|       |          }
 1267|       |          bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] >>= bit_shift;
 1268|       |          bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] |= keystone << bit_overflow;
 1269|       |        }
 1270|       |      }
 1271|       |
 1272|       |      // mask out filler bits
 1273|       |      if constexpr ((bool)LAST_BIT) {
 1274|       |        bit_set[NUM_FIELDS - 1] &= MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
 1275|       |      }
 1276|       |
 1277|       |      return *this;
 1278|       |
 1279|       |    }

 1289|       |    /// Addition of two Bitsets.
 1290|       |    /// Wraps if it overflows.
 1291|       |    /// Returns this object.
 1292|       |    BitSet & ADD_SELF(const BitSet & set2) {
 1293|       |      bool carry = false;
 1294|       |
 1295|       |      for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS; ++i) {
 1296|       |        field_t addend = set2.bit_set[i] + static_cast<field_t>(carry);
 1297|       |        carry = set2.bit_set[i] > addend;
 1298|       |
 1299|       |        field_t sum = bit_set[i] + addend;
 1300|       |        carry |= bit_set[i] > sum;
 1301|       |
 1302|       |        bit_set[i] = sum;
 1303|       |      }
 1304|       |
 1305|       |      if constexpr (static_cast<bool>(LAST_BIT)) {
 1306|       |        bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS] = (
 1307|       |          bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS]
 1308|       |          + set2.bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS]
 1309|       |          + static_cast<field_t>(carry)
 1310|       |        ) & emp::MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
 1311|       |      }
 1312|       |
 1313|       |      return *this;
 1314|       |    }

 1324|       |    /// Subtraction of two Bitsets.
 1325|       |    /// Wraps if it underflows.
 1326|       |    /// Returns this object.
 1327|       |    BitSet & SUB_SELF(const BitSet & set2){
 1328|       |
 1329|       |      bool carry = false;
 1330|       |
 1331|       |      for (size_t i = 0; i < NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS; ++i) {
 1332|       |        field_t subtrahend = set2.bit_set[i] + static_cast<field_t>(carry);
 1333|       |        carry = set2.bit_set[i] > subtrahend;
 1334|       |        carry |= bit_set[i] < subtrahend;
 1335|       |        bit_set[i] -= subtrahend;
 1336|       |     }
 1337|       |
 1338|       |      if constexpr (static_cast<bool>(LAST_BIT)) {
 1339|       |        bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS] = (
 1340|       |          bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS]
 1341|       |          - set2.bit_set[NUM_BITS/FIELD_BITS]
 1342|       |          - static_cast<field_t>(carry)
 1343|       |        ) & emp::MaskLow<field_t>(LAST_BIT);
 1344|       |      }
 1345|       |
 1346|       |      return *this;
 1347|       |    }

 1418|       |    template <class Archive>
 1419|       |    void serialize( Archive & ar )
 1420|       |    {
 1421|       |      if constexpr ( sizeof(field_t) != sizeof(uint64_t) ) {
 1422|       |        // in order for JSON serialization interoperability of native (64-bit)
 1423|       |        // and emscripten (32-bit) artifacts,
 1424|       |        // in 32-bit mode we have serialize as an array of 64-bit values
 1425|       |        uint64_t buf[ (sizeof(bit_set) + 7) / 8 ]{};
 1426|       |        std::memcpy( buf, bit_set, sizeof(bit_set) ); // copy to buf
 1427|       |        ar( buf );
 1428|       |        std::memcpy( bit_set, buf, sizeof(bit_set) ); // copy from buf
 1429|       |      } else {
 1430|       |        ar( bit_set );
 1431|       |      }
 1432|       |    }

  777|      0|      for (size_t i = index; i < index + num; i++) this->Set(i, val);

  795|       |
  796|       |    /// Return the position of the first one after start_pos; return -1 if no ones in vector.
  797|       |    /// You can loop through all 1-bit positions of a BitVector "bv" with:
  798|       |    ///
  799|       |    ///   for (int pos = bv.FindBit(); pos >= 0; pos = bv.FindBit(pos+1)) { ... }
  800|       |
  801|      0|    int FindBit(const size_t start_pos) const {
  802|      0|      if (start_pos >= num_bits) return -1;

  806|      0|        return (int) (find_bit(bit_set[field_id] & ~(emp::MaskLow<field_t>(field_pos))) +
  807|      0|                      field_id * FIELD_BITS);
  808|      0|      }
  809|      0|
  810|      0|      // Search other fields...

  240|       |    while (S != E) {
  241|       |      --E;
  242|       |      E->~T();
  243|       |    }

  246|       |  /// Move the range [I, E) into the uninitialized memory starting with "Dest",
  247|       |  /// constructing elements as needed.

  250|       |    std::uninitialized_copy(std::make_move_iterator(I),
  251|       |                            std::make_move_iterator(E), Dest);
  252|       |  }
  253|       |
  254|       |  /// Copy the range [I, E) onto the uninitialized memory starting with "Dest",
  255|       |  /// constructing elements as needed.

  258|       |    std::uninitialized_copy(I, E, Dest);

  270|       |    this->set_size(this->size() + 1);

  276|       |    this->set_size(this->size() + 1);

  285|       |// Define this out-of-line to dissuade the C++ compiler from inlining it.
  286|       |template <typename T, bool TriviallyCopyable>
  287|       |void SmallVectorTemplateBase<T, TriviallyCopyable>::grow(size_t MinSize) {
  288|       |
  289|       |  // if (MinSize > UINT32_MAX)
  290|       |  //   report_bad_alloc_error("SmallVector capacity overflow during allocation");
  291|       |
  292|       |  // Always grow, even from zero.
  293|       |  size_t NewCapacity = size_t(emp::NextPowerOf2(this->capacity() + 2));
  294|       |  NewCapacity = std::min(std::max(NewCapacity, MinSize), size_t(UINT32_MAX));
  295|       |  T *NewElts = static_cast<T*>(malloc(NewCapacity*sizeof(T)));
  296|       |
  297|       |  // Move the elements over.
  298|       |  this->uninitialized_move(this->begin(), this->end(), NewElts);
  299|       |
  300|       |  // Destroy the original elements.
  301|       |  destroy_range(this->begin(), this->end());
  302|       |
  303|       |  // If this wasn't grown from the inline copy, deallocate the old space.
  304|       |  if (!this->isSmall())

   59|       |  /// Implementation of the murmur3 hash, a fast hash with low collisions.
   60|       |  /// This hash makes it suitable for hash-based lookups.
   61|       |  /// For more info, see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MurmurHash
   62|       |  /// This implementation was directly based on:
   63|       |  /// https://github.com/aappleby/smhasher/blob/92cf3702fcfaadc84eb7bef59825a23e0cd84f56/src/MurmurHash3.cpp
   64|       |  /// @param key Span of bytes to hash.
   65|       |  /// @param seed Optional seed.
   66|       |  /// @return Hash of key.
   67|       |  constexpr inline size_t murmur_hash(
   68|       |    const std::span<const std::byte> key,
   69|       |    const size_t seed = 0
   70|      0|  ) {

   72|      0|    const size_t numbytes = key.size();

   75|      0|    const uint64_t c2 = 0x4cf5ad432745937fLLU;

   83|      0|      uint64_t ret{0};

   85|      0|      return ret;

  114|      0|    uint64_t k2 = 0;

  166|       |  /// This structure serves as a hash for containers that are iterable.
  167|       |  /// Use as a drop-in replacement for std::hash.
  168|       |  template <typename Container, size_t Seed = 0>
  169|       |  struct ContainerHash
  170|       |  {

   90|       |
   91|       |    using query_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
   92|       |    using tag_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
   93|       |
   94|       |    size_t dim() const override { return 1; }
   95|       |
   96|       |    size_t width() const override { return Width; }
   97|       |

   99|       |      return emp::to_string(Width) + "-bit " + base();
  100|       |    }
  101|       |
  102|       |    std::string base() const override { return "Hash Metric"; }
  103|       |
  104|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  105|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  106|       |    }
  107|       |
  108|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  109|       |      std::hash<query_t> qhasher;
  110|       |      std::hash<tag_t> thasher;
  111|       |
  112|       |      size_t input[2]{qhasher(a), thasher(b)};
  113|       |      const std::span<const std::byte> input_as_bytes(
  114|       |          reinterpret_cast<std::byte*>(input),
  115|       |          sizeof(input)
  116|       |      );
  117|       |      const size_t hash = emp::murmur_hash(input_as_bytes);
  118|       |      return static_cast<double>(hash) / static_cast<double>(std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max());
  119|       |    }

  125|       |  /// Generate an arbitrary, but consistent, match score between 0 and 1
  126|       |  /// Be sure to link against -lcrypto, -lssl, and provide -DEMP_HAS_CRYPTO
  127|       |  template<size_t Width>
  128|       |  struct CryptoHashMetric: public BaseMetric<emp::BitSet<Width>, emp::BitSet<Width>> {
  129|       |
  130|       |    using query_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  131|       |    using tag_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  132|       |
  133|       |    size_t dim() const override { return 1; }
  134|       |
  135|       |    size_t width() const override { return Width; }
  136|       |
  137|       |    std::string name() const override {
  138|       |      return emp::to_string(Width) + "-bit " + base();
  139|       |    }
  140|       |
  141|       |    std::string base() const override { return "Hash Metric"; }
  142|       |
  143|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  144|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  145|       |    }
  146|       |
  147|       |    // adapted from https://www.uncg.edu/cmp/faculty/srtate/580.f11/sha1examples.php
  148|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  149|       |
  150|       |    std::array<unsigned char, a.GetNumBytes() + b.GetNumBytes()> data;
  151|       |
  152|       |    size_t i = 0;
  153|       |    for (size_t j = 0; j < a.GetNumBytes(); ++j) data[i++] = a.GetByte(j);
  154|       |    for (size_t j = 0; j < b.GetNumBytes(); ++j) data[i++] = b.GetByte(j);
  155|       |
  156|       |    SHA_CTX shactx;
  157|       |    std::array<unsigned char, SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH> digest;
  158|       |
  159|       |    SHA1_Init(&shactx);
  160|       |    SHA1_Update(&shactx, data.data(), data.size());
  161|       |    SHA1_Final(digest.data(), &shactx);
  162|       |
  163|       |    const std::string hashme{
  164|       |      reinterpret_cast<const char *>(digest.data()),
  165|       |      digest.size()
  166|       |    };
  167|       |
  168|       |    return (
  169|       |      static_cast<double>(std::hash<std::string>{}(hashme))
  170|       |      / std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max()
  171|       |    );
  172|       |
  173|       |  }
  174|       |
  175|       |  };
  176|       |  #endif

  211|       |  struct NextUpMetric : public BaseMetric<size_t, size_t> {

  227|       |

  229|       |      const size_t difference = ((Max + 1) + b - a) % (Max + 1);
  230|       |      return static_cast<double>(difference % (Max + 1)) / Max;

  294|       |  /// Adapted from Downing, Keith L. Intelligence emerging: adaptivity and search in evolving neural systems. MIT Press, 2015.
  295|       |  template<size_t Width>
  296|       |  struct SymmetricWrapMetric : public BaseMetric<emp::BitSet<Width>, emp::BitSet<Width>> {
  297|       |
  298|       |    using query_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  299|       |    using tag_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  300|       |
  301|       |    size_t dim() const override { return 1; }
  302|       |
  303|       |    size_t width() const override { return Width; }
  304|       |
  305|       |    std::string name() const override {
  306|       |      return emp::to_string(Width) + "-bit " + base();
  307|       |    }
  308|       |
  309|       |    std::string base() const override { return "Symmetric Wrap Metric"; }
  310|       |
  311|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  312|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  313|       |    }
  314|       |
  315|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  316|       |      constexpr double max_dist = (
  317|       |        (emp::BitSet<Width>::MaxDouble() + 1.0) / 2.0
  318|       |      );
  319|       |      return std::min(a - b, b - a).GetDouble() / max_dist;
  320|       |    }
  321|       |
  322|       |  };

  355|       |  /// Matches based on the number of bits in common between the two bitsets.
  356|       |  /// Normalized so that each match score represents the cumulative probability
  357|       |  /// of an as-good or better match.
  358|       |  template<size_t Width>
  359|       |  struct HammingCumuMetric : public BaseMetric<emp::BitSet<Width>, emp::BitSet<Width>> {
  360|       |
  361|       |    struct static_constructed : public emp::vector<double> {
  362|       |
  363|       |      static_constructed() {
  364|       |        double cumsum = 0.0;
  365|       |        emp::Binomial bino(0.5, Width);
  366|       |        while (this->size() <= Width) {
  367|       |          cumsum += bino[this->size()];
  368|       |          this->push_back(cumsum);
  369|       |        }
  370|       |      }
  371|       |
  372|       |    };
  373|       |
  374|       |    inline static static_constructed cumulative{};
  375|       |
  376|       |    using query_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  377|       |    using tag_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  378|       |
  379|       |    size_t dim() const override { return 1; }
  380|       |
  381|       |    size_t width() const override { return Width; }
  382|       |
  383|       |    std::string name() const override {
  384|       |      return emp::to_string(Width) + "-bit " + base();
  385|       |    }
  386|       |
  387|       |    std::string base() const override { return "Cumulative Hamming Metric"; }
  388|       |
  389|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  390|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  391|       |    }
  392|       |
  393|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  394|       |
  395|       |      return cumulative[(a^b).CountOnes()];
  396|       |
  397|       |    }
  398|       |
  399|       |  };

  413|       |

  429|       |      const emp::BitSet<Width> bs = a^b;
  430|       |      const size_t same = (~bs).LongestSegmentOnes();

  432|       |
  433|       |      return ps;
  434|       |    }
  435|       |
  436|       |    static inline double ProbabilityKBitSequence(const size_t k) {
  437|       |      const double numerator = static_cast<double>(Width - k + 1);
  438|       |
  439|       |      double denominator;
  440|       |      if constexpr (Width < 511) {
  441|       |        emp_assert(k < 511);
  442|       |        denominator = emp::exp2_overflow_unsafe(-static_cast<int>(k));
  443|       |      } else {
  444|       |        denominator = emp::exp2(-static_cast<int>(k));
  445|       |      }
  446|       |
  447|       |      // Bad Math
  448|       |      // ... at least clamp it
  449|       |      return std::clamp(numerator * denominator, 0.0, 1.0);
  450|       |
  451|       |    }
  452|       |
  453|       |  };

  527|       |  /// Compute the probability of K or more heads in a row out of N flips.
  528|       |  /// Adapted from https://www.askamathematician.com/2010/07/q-whats-the-chance-of-getting-a-run-of-k-successes-in-n-bernoulli-trials-why-use-approximations-when-the-exact-answer-is-known/
  529|       |  /// Helper class for exact streak metrics
  530|       |  template<size_t N>
  531|       |  struct ExactStreakDistribution {
  532|       |
  533|       |    robin_hood::unordered_map<
  534|       |      std::tuple<size_t, size_t>, /* (min_heads, num_coins) */
  535|       |      double,
  536|       |      emp::TupleHash<size_t, size_t>
  537|       |    > computed{};
  538|       |
  539|       |    ExactStreakDistribution() {
  540|       |      // prep the cache
  541|       |      for (size_t min_heads = 0; min_heads <= N; ++min_heads) {
  542|       |        CalcStreakProbability(min_heads);
  543|       |      }
  544|       |    }
  545|       |
  546|       |    double GetStreakProbability(
  547|       |      const size_t min_heads,
  548|       |      const size_t num_coins=N
  549|       |    ) const { return computed.at({min_heads, num_coins}); }
  550|       |
  551|       |    double CalcStreakProbability(
  552|       |      const size_t min_heads,
  553|       |      const size_t num_coins=N
  554|       |    ) {
  555|       |
  556|       |      // edge cases for recursion
  557|       |      if (min_heads > num_coins || num_coins <= 0) return 0.0;
  558|       |
  559|       |      // check the cache
  560|       |      if (computed.find({min_heads, num_coins}) != std::end(computed)) {
  561|       |        return computed.at({min_heads, num_coins});
  562|       |      }
  563|       |
  564|       |      constexpr double head_prob = 0.5;
  565|       |
  566|       |      double res = emp::Pow(head_prob, static_cast<double>(min_heads));
  567|       |      for (size_t first_tail = 0; first_tail < min_heads; ++first_tail) {
  568|       |        res += (
  569|       |          emp::Pow(head_prob, static_cast<double>(first_tail))
  570|       |          * (1.0 - head_prob)
  571|       |          * CalcStreakProbability(
  572|       |            min_heads,
  573|       |            num_coins - first_tail - 1
  574|       |          )
  575|       |        );
  576|       |      }
  577|       |
  578|       |      // cache result
  579|       |      computed[{min_heads, num_coins}] = res;
  580|       |
  581|       |      emp_assert(res >= 0.0 && res <= 1.0);
  582|       |
  583|       |      return res;
  584|       |
  585|       |    }
  586|       |
  587|       |  };
  588|       |
  589|       |  // RE: the “static initialization order ‘fiasco’ (problem)”
  590|       |  // https://isocpp.org/wiki/faq/ctors#static-init-order-on-first-use
  591|       |  template<size_t N>
  592|       |  const ExactStreakDistribution<N>&
  593|       |  ExactStreakDistribution_ConstructOnFirstUse() {
  594|       |    static ExactStreakDistribution<N>* res = new ExactStreakDistribution<N>{};
  595|       |    return *res;
  596|       |  }

  647|       |  /// Matches based on longest streak of equal bits in two bitsets.
  648|       |  /// This implementation uses Corect Math adapted from
  649|       |  /// https://www.askamathematician.com/2010/07/q-whats-the-chance-of-getting-a-run-of-k-successes-in-n-bernoulli-trials-why-use-approximations-when-the-exact-answer-is-known/
  650|       |  /// This metric is uniformly distributed.
  651|       |  /// Adapted from Downing, Keith L. Intelligence emerging: adaptivity and search in evolving neural systems. MIT Press, 2015.
  652|       |  template<size_t Width>
  653|       |  struct ExactSingleStreakMetric : public BaseMetric<

  677|       |    }

  680|       |      const size_t same = (a.EQU(b)).LongestSegmentOnes();
  681|       |      // sampling from probabilty distribution
  682|       |      // and then viewing location in cumulative probability distribution
  683|       |      // gives us a uniform result
  684|       |      const double p_same = GetDistn().GetStreakProbability(same);
  685|       |

  687|       |    }
  688|       |

  690|       |
  691|       |  template<size_t Width>
  692|       |  struct CodonMetric : public BaseMetric<
  693|       |    emp::BitSet<Width>,
  694|       |    emp::BitSet<Width>
  695|       |  > {
  696|       |
  697|       |    using query_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  698|       |    using tag_t = emp::BitSet<Width>;
  699|       |
  700|       |    size_t dim() const override { return 1; }
  701|       |
  702|       |    size_t width() const override { return Width; }
  703|       |
  704|       |    std::string name() const override {
  705|       |      return emp::to_string(Width) + "-bit " + base();
  706|       |    }
  707|       |
  708|       |    std::string base() const override { return "Codon Metric"; }
  709|       |
  710|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  711|       |
  712|       |      // codon code
  713|       |      emp::Random rand_(1);
  714|       |      const emp::BitSet<Width> codon_code(rand_);
  715|       |
  716|       |      emp::vector<size_t> query_codon_idxs;
  717|       |      emp::vector<size_t> tag_codon_idxs;
  718|       |      emp::BitSet<Width> mask;
  719|       |      mask.SetUInt(0, 15);
  720|       |      for (size_t i{}; i < Width; i += 4) {
  721|       |        if ((mask & a) == (mask & codon_code)) query_codon_idxs.push_back(i);
  722|       |        if ((mask & b) == (mask & codon_code)) tag_codon_idxs.push_back(i);
  723|       |        const auto temp = mask;
  724|       |        for (size_t j{}; j < 15; ++j) {
  725|       |          mask += temp;
  726|       |        }
  727|       |      }
  728|       |
  729|       |      emp::vector<emp::BitSet<Width>> query_genes;
  730|       |      query_genes.push_back(a);
  731|       |      for (const size_t i : query_codon_idxs) {
  732|       |        query_genes.push_back(a.ROTATE(i + 4));
  733|       |      }
  734|       |
  735|       |      emp::vector<emp::BitSet<Width>> tag_genes;
  736|       |      tag_genes.push_back(b);
  737|       |      for (const size_t i : tag_codon_idxs) {
  738|       |        tag_genes.push_back(b.ROTATE(i + 4));
  739|       |      }
  740|       |
  741|       |      emp::vector<size_t> overlaps;
  742|       |      for (const auto& query_gene : query_genes) {
  743|       |        for (const auto& tag_gene : tag_genes) {
  744|       |          overlaps.push_back(
  745|       |            (query_gene ^ tag_gene).FindBit()
  746|       |          );
  747|       |        }
  748|       |      }
  749|       |
  750|       |      if (overlaps.size()) return 1.0 / static_cast<double>(
  751|       |        *std::max_element(std::begin(overlaps), std::end(overlaps)) + 2
  752|       |      );
  753|       |      else return 1.0;
  754|       |    }
  755|       |
  756|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  757|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  758|       |    }
  759|       |
  760|       |  };
  761|       |
  762|       |  /// Matches based on longest streaks of equal and unequal bits in two bitsets.
  763|       |  /// Adapted from Downing, Keith L. Intelligence emerging: adaptivity and search in evolving neural systems. MIT Press, 2015.
  764|       |  template<size_t Width>
  765|       |  using StreakMetric = ApproxDualStreakMetric<Width>;
  766|       |
  767|       |  template<typename Metric, size_t MaxCapacity=100000>
  768|       |  struct CacheMod : public Metric {
  769|       |
  770|       |    using query_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  771|       |    using tag_t = typename Metric::tag_t;
  772|       |
  773|       |    Metric metric;
  774|       |
  775|       |    static inline robin_hood::unordered_map<
  776|       |      std::tuple<query_t, tag_t>,
  777|       |      double,
  778|       |      emp::TupleHash<query_t, tag_t>
  779|       |    > cache;
  780|       |    static inline std::queue<std::tuple<query_t, tag_t>> purge_queue;
  781|       |
  782|       |    std::string name() const override { return metric.name(); }
  783|       |
  784|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  785|       |
  786|       |      if (cache.find({a, b}) == std::end(cache)) {
  787|       |        // make space if needed
  788|       |        if (cache.size() >= MaxCapacity) {
  789|       |          cache.erase(purge_queue.front());
  790|       |          purge_queue.pop();
  791|       |        }
  792|       |
  793|       |        cache[{a, b}] = Metric::calculate(a, b);
  794|       |        purge_queue.push({a, b});
  795|       |      }
  796|       |
  797|       |      return cache.at({a, b});
  798|       |
  799|       |    }
  800|       |
  801|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  802|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  803|       |    }
  804|       |
  805|       |  };

  881|       |  // Root greater than one squishes probability distribution to the center
  882|       |  // Root less than one flattens out probability distribution
  883|       |  // Root must be positive
  884|       |  template <typename Metric, typename Root>
  885|       |  struct PowMod : public Metric {
  886|       |
  887|       |    using query_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  888|       |    using tag_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  889|       |
  890|       |    Metric metric;
  891|       |
  892|       |    std::string name() const override {
  893|       |      return (
  894|       |        emp::to_string(Root::num) + "/" + emp::to_string(Root::den)
  895|       |        + " Power " + metric.name()
  896|       |      );
  897|       |    }
  898|       |
  899|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  900|       |      constexpr double exp = static_cast<double>(Root::num) / Root::den;
  901|       |      emp_assert(exp > 0);
  902|       |      if constexpr (exp == 1.0) return Metric::calculate(a,b);
  903|       |
  904|       |      const double base = -1.0 + 2.0 * Metric::calculate(a,b);
  905|       |      return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::copysign(std::pow(std::abs(base), exp), base));
  906|       |    }
  907|       |
  908|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  909|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  910|       |    }
  911|       |
  912|       |  };

  914|       |  // Base less than one squishes probability distribution to the center
  915|       |  // Base greater than one flattens out probability distribution
  916|       |  // Base must be positive
  917|       |  template <typename Metric, typename Base>
  918|       |  struct LogMod : public Metric {
  919|       |
  920|       |    using query_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  921|       |    using tag_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  922|       |
  923|       |    Metric metric;
  924|       |
  925|       |    std::string name() const override {
  926|       |      return (
  927|       |        emp::to_string(Base::num) + "/" + emp::to_string(Base::den)
  928|       |        + " Logarithm " + metric.name()
  929|       |      );
  930|       |    }
  931|       |
  932|       |    inline static double calculate(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) {
  933|       |      constexpr double base = static_cast<double>(Base::num) / Base::den;
  934|       |      emp_assert(base > 0);
  935|       |      if constexpr (base == 1.0) return Metric::calculate(a,b);
  936|       |
  937|       |
  938|       |      const double raw = Metric::calculate(a,b) - 0.5;
  939|       |      const double antilog = (
  940|       |        (2 - base)
  941|       |        + 2 * (base - 1) * (std::abs(raw) + 0.5)
  942|       |      );
  943|       |      return 0.5 * (
  944|       |        1.0 + std::copysign(emp::Log(antilog, base), raw)
  945|       |      );
  946|       |    }
  947|       |
  948|       |    double operator()(const query_t& a, const tag_t& b) const override {
  949|       |      return calculate(a, b);
  950|       |    }
  951|       |
  952|       |  };

  957|       |    // accessory to UnifMod
  958|       |    template <typename Metric, size_t Samples>
  959|       |    class EstimatedLookupTable {
  960|       |
  961|       |      using query_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  962|       |      using tag_t = typename Metric::query_t;
  963|       |
  964|       |      // pairs of (raw, uniformified)
  965|       |      emp::vector<std::pair<double, double>> table;
  966|       |
  967|       |    public:
  968|       |      EstimatedLookupTable(const Metric & metric) {
  969|       |        emp::Random rand(1);
  970|       |
  971|       |        emp::vector<double> raw;
  972|       |        emp::vector<double> uniformified;
  973|       |
  974|       |        // true for all metrics
  975|       |        raw.push_back(0.0);
  976|       |        uniformified.push_back(0.0);
  977|       |
  978|       |        // add data
  979|       |        for (size_t i = 0; i < Samples; ++i) {
  980|       |          raw.push_back(metric(query_t(rand), tag_t(rand)));
  981|       |          uniformified.push_back(
  982|       |            // {a} -> {0.5}
  983|       |            // {a,b} -> {0.333, 0.667}
  984|       |            // {a,b,c} -> {0.25, 0.5, 0.75}
  985|       |            // etc.
  986|       |            static_cast<double>(i+1)/static_cast<double>(Samples+1)
  987|       |          );
  988|       |        }
  989|       |
  990|       |        // true for all metrics
  991|       |        raw.push_back(1.0);
  992|       |        uniformified.push_back(1.0);
  993|       |
  994|       |        std::sort(std::begin(raw), std::end(raw));
  995|       |
  996|       |        // zip together
  997|       |        emp::vector<std::pair<double, double>> observations;
  998|       |        std::transform(
  999|       |          std::begin(raw), std::end(raw),
 1000|       |          std::begin(uniformified),
 1001|       |          std::back_inserter(observations),
 1002|       |          [](double r, double u){ return std::pair{r, u}; }
 1003|       |        );
 1004|       |
 1005|       |        // keep only most extreme duplicate observations
 1006|       |        // e.g., if three or more keep bookend two
 1007|       |        for (
 1008|       |          auto front = std::begin(observations);
 1009|       |          front != std::end(observations);
 1010|       |          front = std::upper_bound(
 1011|       |            front,
 1012|       |            std::end(observations),
 1013|       |            *front,
 1014|       |            [](const auto &a, const auto &b){ return a.first < b.first; }
 1015|       |          )
 1016|       |        ) {
 1017|       |
 1018|       |          const auto back = std::upper_bound(
 1019|       |            front,
 1020|       |            std::end(observations),
 1021|       |            *front,
 1022|       |            [](const auto &a, const auto &b){ return a.first < b.first; }
 1023|       |          );
 1024|       |          table.push_back(*front);
 1025|       |          if (
 1026|       |            front != std::prev(back)
 1027|       |          ) table.push_back(*std::prev(back));
 1028|       |
 1029|       |        }
 1030|       |
 1031|       |      }
 1032|       |
 1033|       |      // lookup a raw score to get a uniformified
 1034|       |      double operator()(const double raw) const {
 1035|       |
 1036|       |        emp_assert(raw >= 0.0 && raw <= 1.0);
 1037|       |
 1038|       |        // handle edge cases
 1039|       |        if (raw == 0.0 || raw == 1.0) return raw;
 1040|       |
 1041|       |        // goal: get two exact bookends if we have EXACTLY the raw value
 1042|       |        // stored in the table
 1043|       |        // otherwise, get the less than and greater than value
 1044|       |
 1045|       |        // Returns an iterator pointing to the first element in the range
 1046|       |        // [first, last) that is not less than (i.e. greater or equal to)
 1047|       |        // value, or last if no such element is found.
 1048|       |        auto tail = std::lower_bound(
 1049|       |          std::begin(table),
 1050|       |          std::end(table),
 1051|       |          // lexographic comparison with operator<
 1052|       |          // find the first element that is greater or equal to
 1053|       |          std::pair{raw, std::nan("")},
 1054|       |          [](const auto &a, const auto &b){ return a.first < b.first; }
 1055|       |        );
 1056|       |
 1057|       |        // if we have a good bookend situation
 1058|       |        if (
 1059|       |          tail->first == raw
 1060|       |          && std::next(tail) != std::end(table)
 1061|       |          && tail->first == std::next(tail)->first
 1062|       |        ) ++tail;
 1063|       |
 1064|       |        // we handled edge cases above and added (0.0, 0.0)
 1065|       |        // so tail won't ever be std::begin(table)
 1066|       |        emp_assert(std::begin(table) != tail);
 1067|       |        const auto head = std::prev(tail);
 1068|       |
 1069|       |        // linear interpolation time
 1070|       |        const double raw_frac = (tail->first == head->first) ? 0.5 : (
 1071|       |          (raw - head->first)
 1072|       |          / (tail->first - head->first)
 1073|       |        );
 1074|       |        return raw_frac * (tail->second - head->second) + head->second;
 1075|       |
 1076|       |      }
 1077|       |
 1078|       |    };
 1079|       |
 1080|       |  }

   19|       | *   Create a StringTypeID class that just has a size_t in it BUT includes a cast to std::string

   24|       | *   the first time an ID is created this other static function will store the string associated

   26|       | *   know it will also assign it a unique ID.  The one potential problem is if the run-time version
   27|       | *   is used BEFORE the compile time version.  As such, we need to always make sure to check if a

   63|       |
   64|       |  // Template specialization to maintain full information of a non-empty string as a type.
   65|       |  template <char C1, char... Cs>
   66|       |  struct StringType<C1,Cs...> {
   67|       |    static constexpr char FIRST = C1;             ///< Easy access to first character of string.
   68|       |    constexpr static int SIZE = 1+sizeof...(Cs);  ///< Easy access to string length.
   69|       |
   70|       |    using this_t = StringType<C1,Cs...>;          ///< The type of the current StringType
   71|       |    using pop = StringType<Cs...>;                ///< StringType after removing the first char
   72|       |    template <char C> using push = StringType<C, C1, Cs...>;       ///< Add char to front of string
   73|       |    template <char C> using push_back = StringType<C1, Cs..., C>;  ///< Add char to back of string
   74|       |
   75|       |    /// Does StringType contains the char C?
   76|       |    constexpr static bool Has(char C) { return (C==C1) | pop::Has(C); }
   77|       |
   78|       |    /// Count the number of occurances of char C in StringType.
   79|       |    constexpr static int Count(int C) { return pop::Count(C) + (C==C1); }
   80|       |
   81|       |    /// Determine the position at which C appears in StringType.
   82|       |    constexpr static int GetID(int C) {
   83|       |      if (C==C1) return 0;
   84|       |      if (!Has(C)) return -1;
   85|       |      return (1+pop::GetID(C));
   86|       |    }
   87|       |
   88|       |    /// Function to retrieve number of elements in StringType
   89|       |    constexpr static int GetSize() { return SIZE; }
   90|       |
   91|       |    /// Determine if there are NO chars in an StringType
   92|       |    constexpr static bool IsEmpty() { return false; }
   93|       |
   94|       |    /// Determine if all chars in StringType are different from each other.
   95|       |    constexpr static bool IsUnique() { return pop::IsUnique() && !pop::Has(C1); }
   96|       |
   97|       |    /// Convert this StringType back to an std::string object (note: NOT constexpr)
   98|       |    static std::string ToString() {
   99|       |      std::stringstream ss;
  100|       |      ss << C1;
  101|       |      (ss << ... << Cs);
  102|       |      return ss.str();
  103|       |    }

/home/runner/workspace/third-party/conduit/third-party/Empirical/include/emp/meta/TypePack.hpp:
    1|       |/**
    2|       | *  @note This file is part of Empirical, https://github.com/devosoft/Empirical
    3|       | *  @copyright Copyright (C) Michigan State University, MIT Software license; see doc/LICENSE.md
    4|       | *  @date 2016-2018
    5|       | *
    6|       | *  @file  TypePack.hpp
    7|       | *  @brief A set of types that can be manipulated at compile time (good for metaprogramming)
    8|       | *
    9|       | *  TypePacks are static structues that provide a large set of mechanisms to access and adjust
   10|       | *  the included types.
   11|       | *
   12|       | *  To create a typepack, just pass in zero or more types into the TypePack template.
   13|       | *
   14|       | *    using my_pack = emp::TypePack<int, std::string, double>;
   15|       | *
   16|       | *  After manipulations, you can apply a type pack using the apply<> member template.  E.g.,
   17|       | *
   18|       | *    my_pack::resize<5,char>::reverse::apply<std::tuple> my_tuple;
   19|       | *
   20|       | *  ...would create a variable of type std::tuple<char, char, double, std::string, int>.
   21|       | *
   22|       | *
   23|       | *  Member functions include (all of which are constexpr):
   24|       | *    Has<T>()           - Return true/false: Is T is part of the pack?
   25|       | *    Count<T>()         - Return number of times T is in the pack.
   26|       | *    GetID<T>()         - Return first position of T in the pack, (or -1 if none).
   27|       | *    GetSize()          - Return total number of types in this pack.
   28|       | *    IsEmpty()          - Return true/false: Is this pack empty?
   29|       | *    IsUnique()         - Return true/false: are all types in pack are distinct?
   30|       | *
   31|       | *  Type accessors:
   32|       | *    get<POS>           - Type at position POS in the pack.
   33|       | *    first_t            - Type of first position in the pack.
   34|       | *    last_t             - Type of last position in the pack.
   35|       | *    select<Ps...>      - Create a new pack with types from selected positions.
   36|       | *
   37|       | *  Type manipulations:
   38|       | *    set<POS, T>        - Change type at position POS to T.
   39|       | *    push_front<Ts...>  - Add any number of types Ts to the front of the pack.
   40|       | *    push_back<Ts...>   - Add any number of types Ts to the back of the pack.
   41|       | *    pop                - Pack with first type missing.
   42|       | *    popN<N>            - Pack with first N types missing.
   43|       | *    shrink<N>          - Pack with ONLY first N types.
   44|       | *    resize<N,D>        - Resize pack to N types; if N greater than current size, pad with D.
   45|       | *    merge<P>           - Append all of pack P to the end of this pack.
   46|       | *    find_union<P>      - Join this pack to P, keeping only one of each type.
   47|       | *    reverse            - Reverse the order of types in this pack.
   48|       | *    rotate             - Move the first type in pack to the end.
   49|       | *
   50|       | *  Applications:
   51|       | *    apply<T>           - Take template T and apply these types as its arguments.
   52|       | *    to_function_t<T>   - Convert to a function type, with return type T and arg types from pack.
   53|       | *    filter<FILTER>     - Keep only those types, T, that can legally form FILTER<T> and does not
   54|       | *                         have a FILTER<T>::value == false.
   55|       | *    filter_out<FILTER> - Remove those types, T, that can legally form FILTER<T> and do not have
   56|       | *                         a FILTER<T>::value == false.
   57|       | *    find<FILTER>       - Convert to first type, T, that can legally form FILTER<T> and does not
   58|       | *                         have a FILTER<T>::value == false.
   59|       | *    wrap<WRAPPER>      - Convert to TypePack where all members are run through WRAPPER
   60|       | *
   61|       | *
   62|       | *  Developer notes:
   63|       | *    - GetIDPack could return an ValPack of ALL ID's for a type that appears more than once.
   64|       | */
   65|       |
   66|       |#ifndef EMP_TYPE_PACK_H
   67|       |#define EMP_TYPE_PACK_H
   68|       |
   69|       |#include "meta.hpp"
   70|       |
   71|       |namespace emp {
   72|       |
   73|       |  // Pre-declaration of TypePack

   82|       |    // Create add N copies of the same type to the end of a TypePack.
   83|       |    template <typename START, typename T, int N>
   84|       |    struct tp_pad { using type = typename tp_pad<START,T,N-1>::type::template add<T>; };
