   88|       |    /// Helper for shifting a specified number of types to TypePack T1 from TypePack T2.
   89|       |    /// Example: to shrink, move the specified number of types to empty TypePack and return it.
   90|       |    ///          to merge, move all of one TypePack over to the other and return it.
   91|       |    template <int S, typename T1, typename T2>
   92|       |    struct tp_shift {
   93|       |      using move_t = typename T2::first_t;
   94|       |      using inc_t = typename T1::template add<move_t>;
   95|       |      using dec_t = typename T2::pop;
   96|       |      using type1 = typename tp_shift<S-1, inc_t, dec_t>::type1;
   97|       |      using type2 = typename tp_shift<S-1, inc_t, dec_t>::type2;
   98|       |    };

  101|       |      using type1 = T1;
  102|       |      using type2 = T2;
  103|       |    };

  105|       |    // Filters create a TypePack with the element if the filter is true, empty if false.
  106|       |    template <typename T, bool> struct tp_filter1 { using type=TypePack<T>; };
  107|       |    template <typename T> struct tp_filter1<T,false> { using type=TypePack<>; };
  108|       |
  109|       |    /// Remove types from a TypePack that can't satisfy a filter.
  110|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class FILTER, int N>
  111|       |    struct tp_filter {
  112|       |      using cur_t = typename T::first_t;                                 // Isolate the first type
  113|       |      using other_tp = typename T::pop;                                  // Isolate remaining types
  114|       |      constexpr static bool cur_result = test_type<FILTER,cur_t>();      // Run filter of cur type
  115|       |      using cur_ftp = typename tp_filter1<cur_t, cur_result>::type;      // Use cur type if true
  116|       |      using other_ftp = typename tp_filter<other_tp, FILTER, N-1>::type; // Recurse
  117|       |      using type = typename cur_ftp::template merge< other_ftp >;        // Merge
  118|       |    };
  119|       |
  120|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class FILTER>
  121|       |      struct tp_filter<T,FILTER,0> { using type = TypePack<>; };

  124|       |      using tp_filter_t = typename tp_filter<T,FILTER,T::SIZE>::type;
  125|       |
  126|       |    /// Remove types from a TypePack that DO satisfy a filter.

  128|       |    struct tp_filter_out {
  129|       |      using cur_t = typename T::first_t;                                 // Isolate the first type
  130|       |      using other_tp = typename T::pop;                                  // Isolate remaining types

  132|       |      using cur_ftp = typename tp_filter1<cur_t, !cur_result>::type;     // Use cur type if true
  133|       |      using other_ftp = typename tp_filter_out<other_tp, FILTER, N-1>::type; // Recurse
  134|       |      using type = typename cur_ftp::template merge< other_ftp >;        // Merge
  135|       |    };

  137|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class FILTER>
  138|       |      struct tp_filter_out<T,FILTER,0> { using type = TypePack<>; };

  140|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class FILTER>
  141|       |      using tp_filter_out_t = typename tp_filter_out<T,FILTER,T::SIZE>::type;
  142|       |
  143|       |    // Wrappers create a TypePack with the wrapped element if the filter is true, empty if false.
  144|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class W, bool> struct tp_wrap1
  145|       |      { using type=TypePack<W<T>>; };
  146|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class W> struct tp_wrap1<T,W,false>
  147|       |      { using type=TypePack<>; };

  149|       |    /// Wrap all types in a TypePack in a template; remove any that can't be wrapped.
  150|       |    template <typename T, template <typename...> class W, int N> struct tp_wrap {
  151|       |      using cur_t = typename T::first_t;                               // Isolate the first type
  152|       |      using other_tp = typename T::pop;                                // Isolate remaining types
  153|       |      constexpr static bool cur_result = test_type<W,cur_t>();         // Use wrap to filter cur type
  154|       |      using cur_ftp = typename tp_wrap1<cur_t, W, cur_result>::type;   // Use cur type if true
  155|       |      using other_ftp = typename tp_wrap<other_tp, W, N-1>::type;      // Recurse
  156|       |      using type = typename cur_ftp::template merge< other_ftp >;      // Merge
  157|       |    };

  163|       |
  164|       |    // Tools to build all combinations of types from a TypePack
  165|       |    template <size_t size,
  166|       |              typename ALL_OPTIONS,
  167|       |              typename CUR_OPTIONS>
  168|       |    struct all_combos {
  169|       |      // Determine combinations for one level smaller.
  170|       |      using next_combos = typename all_combos<size-1, ALL_OPTIONS, ALL_OPTIONS>::result_t;
  171|       |
  172|       |      using cur_type = typename CUR_OPTIONS::first_t;
  173|       |      using next_options = typename CUR_OPTIONS::pop;
  174|       |      template <typename T>
  175|       |      using push_wrap = typename T::template push_back<cur_type>;
  176|       |
  177|       |      // pushed_types is the set of currently-built types with the FIRST option added on.
  178|       |      using pushed_types = typename next_combos::template wrap<push_wrap>;
  179|       |
  180|       |      // other_results is the set of currently built types with the OTHER options added on.
  181|       |      using other_results = typename all_combos<size, ALL_OPTIONS, next_options>::result_t;
  182|       |
  183|       |      // cur_result_t is the merger of pushed_type and other types (i.e., ALL types added on)
  184|       |      using result_t = typename pushed_types::template merge<other_results>;
  185|       |    };

  188|       |    template <size_t size,

  191|       |      using result_t = emp::TypePack<>;
  192|       |    };

  197|       |      using result_t = emp::TypePack<emp::TypePack<>>;

  106|       |    template <typename T> struct vp_sort;
  107|       |    template <auto V1, auto... Vs> struct vp_sort<ValPack<V1, Vs...>> {
  108|       |      using vp = ValPack<V1, Vs...>;
  109|       |      using result = typename vp_sort_impl<vp, ValPack<>>::template sort<vp::Min()>;
  110|       |    };
  111|       |    template <> struct vp_sort<ValPack<>> { using result = ValPack<>; };
  112|       |  } // End internal namespace
  113|       |  #endif // DOXYGEN_SHOULD_SKIP_THIS
  114|       |
  115|       |  /// Generate a ValPack with a specified range of values.
  116|       |  template <auto START, auto END, auto STEP=1>
  117|       |  using ValPackRange = typename internal::vp_range<(START >= END), START, END, STEP>::type;
  118|       |
  119|       |  /// Generate a count from 0 to COUNT-1 (so a total of COUNT values)
  120|       |  template <auto COUNT>
  121|       |  using ValPackCount = ValPackRange<0, COUNT, 1>;
  122|       |
  123|       |  /// ValPack with at least one value.
  124|       |  template <auto V1, auto... Vs>
  125|       |  struct ValPack<V1,Vs...> {
  126|       |    /// First value in ValPack
  127|       |    static constexpr auto first = V1;
  128|       |
  129|       |    /// Number of values in ValPack
  130|       |    constexpr static size_t SIZE = 1+sizeof...(Vs);
  131|       |
  132|       |    using this_t = ValPack<V1,Vs...>;
  133|       |    using pop = ValPack<Vs...>;
  134|       |
  135|       |    /// Add a value to the front of an ValPack
  136|       |    template <auto V> using push = ValPack<V, V1, Vs...>;
  137|       |
  138|       |    /// Add a value to the back of an ValPack
  139|       |    template <auto V> using push_back = ValPack<V1, Vs..., V>;
  140|       |
  141|       |    /// Push V onto front of an ValPack if it does not equal X
  142|       |    template <auto V, auto X> using push_if_not = typename internal::vp_push_if_not<V,X,this_t>::result;
  143|       |
  144|       |    /// Push V onto back of an ValPack if it does not equal X
  145|       |    template <auto V, auto X> using push_back_if_not = typename internal::vp_push_if_not<V,X,this_t>::back;
  146|       |
  147|       |    /// Remove the first time value V appears from an ValPack
  148|       |    template <auto V> using pop_val = typename internal::vp_loop<this_t, ValPack<>, false, 2>::template pop_val<V>;
  149|       |
  150|       |    /// Remove the all appearances of value V from an ValPack
  151|       |    template <auto V> using remove = typename internal::vp_loop<this_t, ValPack<>, false, 3>::template remove<V>;
  152|       |
  153|       |    /// Append one whole ValPack to the end of another.
  154|       |    template <typename T> using append = typename internal::vp_concat<this_t,T>::result;
  155|       |
  156|       |    /// Apply to a specified template with ValPack as template arguments.
  157|       |    template <template <int...> class TEMPLATE> using apply = TEMPLATE<V1, Vs...>;
  158|       |
  159|       |
  160|       |    /// ---=== Member Functions ===---
  161|       |
  162|       |    /// Return wheter an ValPack contains the value V.
  163|       |    template <typename T>
  164|       |    constexpr static bool Has(T val) { return (val==V1) | pop::Has(val); }
  165|       |
  166|       |    /// Count the number of occurances of value V in ValPack.
  167|       |    template <typename T>
  168|       |    constexpr static size_t Count(T val) { return pop::Count(val) + (val==V1); }
  169|       |
  170|       |    /// Determine the position at which V appears in ValPack.
  171|       |    template <typename T>
  172|       |    constexpr static int GetID(T val) { return (val==V1) ? 0 : (1+pop::GetID(val)); }
  173|       |
  174|       |    /// Function to retrieve number of elements in ValPack
  175|       |    constexpr static size_t GetSize() { return SIZE; }
  176|       |
  177|       |    /// Determine if there are NO value in an ValPack
  178|       |    constexpr static bool IsEmpty() { return false; }
  179|       |
  180|       |    /// Determine if all values in ValPack are different from each other.
  181|       |    constexpr static bool IsUnique() { return pop::IsUnique() && !pop::Has(V1); }
  182|       |
  183|       |    /// Add up all values in an ValPack
  184|       |    constexpr static auto Sum() { return V1 + pop::Sum(); }
  185|       |
  186|       |    /// Multiply together all value in an ValPack
  187|       |    constexpr static auto Product() { return V1 * pop::Product(); }
  188|       |
  189|       |    /// Find the smallest value in an ValPack, to a maximum of cap.
  190|       |    template <typename T>
  191|       |    constexpr static auto Min(T cap) { return cap < pop::Min(V1) ? cap : pop::Min(V1); }
  192|       |
  193|       |    /// Find the overall smallest value in an ValPack
  194|       |    constexpr static auto Min() { return pop::Min(V1); }
  195|       |
  196|       |    /// Find the maximum value in an ValPack, to a minimum of floor.
  197|       |    template <typename T>
  198|       |    constexpr static auto Max(T floor) { return floor > pop::Max(V1) ? floor : pop::Max(V1); }
  199|       |
  200|       |    /// Find the overall maximum value in an ValPack.
  201|       |    constexpr static auto Max() { return pop::Max(V1); }
  202|       |
  203|       |    /// Use each value in an ValPack as an index and return results as a tuple.
  204|       |    template <typename T>
  205|       |    constexpr static auto ApplyIndex(T && container) {
  206|       |      return std::make_tuple(container[V1], container[Vs]...);
  207|       |    }
  208|       |
  209|       |    /// Convert all values from an ValPack into a string, treating each as a char.
  210|       |    static std::string ToString() {
  211|       |      return std::string(1, (char) V1) + pop::ToString();
  212|       |    }
  213|       |
  214|       |    /// Print all values in an ValPack into a stream.
  215|       |    static void PrintVals(std::ostream & os=std::cout) {
  216|       |      os << V1;
  217|       |      if (GetSize() > 1) os << ',';
  218|       |      pop::PrintVals(os);
  219|       |    }
  220|       |  };
  221|       |
  222|       |  // ValPack with no values.
  223|       |  template <> struct ValPack<> {
  224|       |    using this_t = ValPack<>;
  225|       |
  226|       |    template <auto V> using push = ValPack<V>;
  227|       |    template <auto V> using push_back = ValPack<V>;
  228|       |    template <auto V, auto X> using push_if_not = typename internal::vp_push_if_not<V,X,ValPack<>>::result;
  229|       |    template <auto V, auto X> using push_back_if_not = typename internal::vp_push_if_not<V,X,ValPack<>>::back;
  230|       |    template <auto V> using pop_val = ValPack<>;  // No value to pop!  Faulure?
  231|       |    template <auto V> using remove = ValPack<>;
  232|       |    template <typename T> using append = T;
  233|       |
  234|       |    template <typename T>
  235|       |    constexpr static bool Has(T) { return false; }
  236|       |    template <typename T>
  237|       |    constexpr static size_t Count(T) { return 0; }
  238|       |    template <typename T>
  239|       |    constexpr static int GetID(T) { return -100000; }
  240|       |
  241|       |    constexpr static size_t SIZE = 0;
  242|      0|    constexpr static size_t GetSize() { return 0; }
  243|       |
  244|      0|    constexpr static bool IsEmpty() { return true; }
  245|      0|    constexpr static bool IsUnique() { return true; }
  246|       |
  247|      0|    constexpr static double Sum() { return 0.0; }
  248|      0|    constexpr static double Product() { return 1.0; }
  249|       |    template <typename T>
  250|       |    constexpr static auto Min(T cap) { return cap; }
  251|       |    template <typename T>
  252|       |    constexpr static auto Max(T floor) { return floor; }
  253|       |
  254|      0|    static std::string ToString() { return ""; }
  255|       |
  256|      0|    static void PrintVals(std::ostream & os=std::cout) { ; }

  261|       |    template <typename T> using uniq = typename internal::vp_uniq<T>::result;

  140|       |  template<bool encode_space=false>
  141|       |  std::string url_encode(const std::string &value) {
  142|       |    std::ostringstream escaped;
  143|       |    escaped.fill('0');
  144|       |    escaped << std::hex;
  145|       |
  146|       |    for (const auto c : value) {
  147|       |
  148|       |      // If encoding space, replace with +
  149|       |      if ( encode_space && c == ' ' ) escaped << '+';
  150|       |      // Keep alphanumeric and other accepted characters intact
  151|       |      else if (
  152|       |        std::isalnum(c) || c == '-' || c == '_' || c == '.' || c == '~'
  153|       |      ) escaped << c;
  154|       |      // Any other characters are percent-encoded
  155|       |      else {
  156|       |        escaped << std::uppercase;
  157|       |        escaped << '%' << std::setw(2) << static_cast<unsigned char>(c);
  158|       |        escaped << std::nouppercase;
  159|       |      }
  160|       |
  161|       |    }
  162|       |
  163|       |    return escaped.str();
  164|       |  }

  172|       |
  173|       |    for (size_t i{}; i < str.size(); ++i) {
  174|       |      if (str[i] == '%') {
  175|       |        int hex_code;

  177|       |        res += static_cast<char>(hex_code);
  178|       |        i += 2;
  179|       |      } else res += ( decode_plus && str[i] == '+' )
  180|       |        ? ' '
  181|       |        : str[i]
  182|       |      ;
  183|       |    }
  184|       |

 1102|       |  /// Apply sprintf-like formatting to a string.
 1103|       |  /// See https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/io/c/fprintf.
 1104|       |  /// Adapted from https://stackoverflow.com/a/26221725.
 1105|       |  template<typename... Args>
 1106|       |  std::string format_string( const std::string& format, Args... args ) {
 1107|       |
 1108|       |    #pragma GCC diagnostic push
 1109|       |    #pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wformat-security"
 1110|       |
 1111|       |    // Extra space for '\0'
 1112|       |    const size_t size = std::snprintf(nullptr, 0, format.c_str(), args...) + 1;
 1113|       |    emp_assert( size >= 0 );
 1114|       |
 1115|       |    emp::vector<char> buf( size );
 1116|       |    std::snprintf( buf.data(), size, format.c_str(), args... );
 1117|       |
 1118|       |     // We don't want the '\0' inside
 1119|       |    return std::string( buf.data(), buf.data() + size - 1 );
 1120|       |
 1121|       |    #pragma GCC diagnostic pop
 1122|       |
 1123|       |  }

  240|       |template <class T, T... Ints>
  241|       |class integer_sequence {
  242|       |public:
  243|       |    using value_type = T;
  244|       |    static_assert(std::is_integral<value_type>::value, "not integral type");
  245|       |    static constexpr std::size_t size() noexcept {
  246|       |        return sizeof...(Ints);
  247|       |    }
  248|       |};
  249|       |template <std::size_t... Inds>
  250|       |using index_sequence = integer_sequence<std::size_t, Inds...>;
  251|       |
  252|       |namespace detail_ {
  253|       |template <class T, T Begin, T End, bool>
  254|       |struct IntSeqImpl {
  255|       |    using TValue = T;
  256|       |    static_assert(std::is_integral<TValue>::value, "not integral type");
  257|       |    static_assert(Begin >= 0 && Begin < End, "unexpected argument (Begin<0 || Begin<=End)");
  258|       |
  259|       |    template <class, class>
  260|       |    struct IntSeqCombiner;
  261|       |
  262|       |    template <TValue... Inds0, TValue... Inds1>
  263|       |    struct IntSeqCombiner<integer_sequence<TValue, Inds0...>, integer_sequence<TValue, Inds1...>> {
  264|       |        using TResult = integer_sequence<TValue, Inds0..., Inds1...>;
  265|       |    };
  266|       |
  267|       |    using TResult =
  268|       |        typename IntSeqCombiner<typename IntSeqImpl<TValue, Begin, Begin + (End - Begin) / 2,
  269|       |                                                    (End - Begin) / 2 == 1>::TResult,
  270|       |                                typename IntSeqImpl<TValue, Begin + (End - Begin) / 2, End,
  271|       |                                                    (End - Begin + 1) / 2 == 1>::TResult>::TResult;
  272|       |};
  273|       |
  274|       |template <class T, T Begin>
  275|       |struct IntSeqImpl<T, Begin, Begin, false> {
  276|       |    using TValue = T;
  277|       |    static_assert(std::is_integral<TValue>::value, "not integral type");
  278|       |    static_assert(Begin >= 0, "unexpected argument (Begin<0)");
  279|       |    using TResult = integer_sequence<TValue>;
  280|       |};
  281|       |
  282|       |template <class T, T Begin, T End>
  283|       |struct IntSeqImpl<T, Begin, End, true> {
  284|       |    using TValue = T;
  285|       |    static_assert(std::is_integral<TValue>::value, "not integral type");
  286|       |    static_assert(Begin >= 0, "unexpected argument (Begin<0)");
  287|       |    using TResult = integer_sequence<TValue, Begin>;
  288|       |};
  289|       |} // namespace detail_

  291|       |template <class T, T N>

  293|       |

  295|       |using make_index_sequence = make_integer_sequence<std::size_t, N>;

  331|       |// make sure this is not inlined as it is slow and dramatically enlarges code, thus making other
  332|       |// inlinings more difficult. Throws are also generally the slow path.
  333|       |template <typename E, typename... Args>
  334|       |[[noreturn]] ROBIN_HOOD(NOINLINE)
  335|       |#if ROBIN_HOOD(HAS_EXCEPTIONS)
  336|      0|    void doThrow(Args&&... args) {
  337|       |    // NOLINTNEXTLINE(cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-array-to-pointer-decay)
  338|      0|    throw E(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  339|      0|}

  342|       |    abort();
  343|       |}
  344|       |#endif

  349|      0|        doThrow<E>(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  350|      0|    }

  355|      0|inline T unaligned_load(void const* ptr) noexcept {
  356|       |    // using memcpy so we don't get into unaligned load problems.
  357|       |    // compiler should optimize this very well anyways.

  362|       |
  363|       |// Allocates bulks of memory for objects of type T. This deallocates the memory in the destructor,
  364|       |// and keeps a linked list of the allocated memory around. Overhead per allocation is the size of a
  365|       |// pointer.
  366|       |template <typename T, size_t MinNumAllocs = 4, size_t MaxNumAllocs = 256>
  367|       |class BulkPoolAllocator {
  368|       |public:
  369|       |    BulkPoolAllocator() noexcept = default;
  370|       |
  371|       |    // does not copy anything, just creates a new allocator.
  372|       |    BulkPoolAllocator(const BulkPoolAllocator& ROBIN_HOOD_UNUSED(o) /*unused*/) noexcept
  373|       |        : mHead(nullptr)
  374|       |        , mListForFree(nullptr) {}
  375|       |
  376|       |    BulkPoolAllocator(BulkPoolAllocator&& o) noexcept
  377|       |        : mHead(o.mHead)
  378|       |        , mListForFree(o.mListForFree) {
  379|       |        o.mListForFree = nullptr;
  380|       |        o.mHead = nullptr;
  381|       |    }
  382|       |
  383|       |    BulkPoolAllocator& operator=(BulkPoolAllocator&& o) noexcept {
  384|       |        reset();
  385|       |        mHead = o.mHead;
  386|       |        mListForFree = o.mListForFree;
  387|       |        o.mListForFree = nullptr;
  388|       |        o.mHead = nullptr;
  389|       |        return *this;
  390|       |    }
  391|       |
  392|       |    BulkPoolAllocator&
  393|       |    // NOLINTNEXTLINE(bugprone-unhandled-self-assignment,cert-oop54-cpp)
  394|       |    operator=(const BulkPoolAllocator& ROBIN_HOOD_UNUSED(o) /*unused*/) noexcept {
  395|       |        // does not do anything
  396|       |        return *this;
  397|       |    }
  398|       |
  399|       |    ~BulkPoolAllocator() noexcept {
  400|       |        reset();
  401|       |    }
  402|       |
  403|       |    // Deallocates all allocated memory.
  404|       |    void reset() noexcept {
  405|       |        while (mListForFree) {
  406|       |            T* tmp = *mListForFree;
  407|       |            ROBIN_HOOD_LOG("std::free")
  408|       |            std::free(mListForFree);
  409|       |            mListForFree = reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<T**>(tmp);
  410|       |        }
  411|       |        mHead = nullptr;
  412|       |    }
  413|       |
  414|       |    // allocates, but does NOT initialize. Use in-place new constructor, e.g.
  415|       |    //   T* obj = pool.allocate();
  416|       |    //   ::new (static_cast<void*>(obj)) T();
  417|       |    T* allocate() {
  418|       |        T* tmp = mHead;
  419|       |        if (!tmp) {
  420|       |            tmp = performAllocation();
  421|       |        }
  422|       |
  423|       |        mHead = *reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<T**>(tmp);
  424|       |        return tmp;
  425|       |    }
  426|       |
  427|       |    // does not actually deallocate but puts it in store.
  428|       |    // make sure you have already called the destructor! e.g. with
  429|       |    //  obj->~T();
  430|       |    //  pool.deallocate(obj);
  431|       |    void deallocate(T* obj) noexcept {
  432|       |        *reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<T**>(obj) = mHead;
  433|       |        mHead = obj;
  434|       |    }
  435|       |
  436|       |    // Adds an already allocated block of memory to the allocator. This allocator is from now on
  437|       |    // responsible for freeing the data (with free()). If the provided data is not large enough to
  438|       |    // make use of, it is immediately freed. Otherwise it is reused and freed in the destructor.
  439|       |    void addOrFree(void* ptr, const size_t numBytes) noexcept {
  440|       |        // calculate number of available elements in ptr
  441|       |        if (numBytes < ALIGNMENT + ALIGNED_SIZE) {
  442|       |            // not enough data for at least one element. Free and return.
  443|       |            ROBIN_HOOD_LOG("std::free")
  444|       |            std::free(ptr);
  445|       |        } else {
  446|       |            ROBIN_HOOD_LOG("add to buffer")
  447|       |            add(ptr, numBytes);
  448|       |        }
  449|       |    }
  450|       |
  451|       |    void swap(BulkPoolAllocator<T, MinNumAllocs, MaxNumAllocs>& other) noexcept {
  452|       |        using std::swap;
  453|       |        swap(mHead, other.mHead);
  454|       |        swap(mListForFree, other.mListForFree);
  455|       |    }
  456|       |
  457|       |private:
  458|       |    // iterates the list of allocated memory to calculate how many to alloc next.
  459|       |    // Recalculating this each time saves us a size_t member.
  460|       |    // This ignores the fact that memory blocks might have been added manually with addOrFree. In
  461|       |    // practice, this should not matter much.
  462|       |    ROBIN_HOOD(NODISCARD) size_t calcNumElementsToAlloc() const noexcept {
  463|       |        auto tmp = mListForFree;
  464|       |        size_t numAllocs = MinNumAllocs;
  465|       |
  466|       |        while (numAllocs * 2 <= MaxNumAllocs && tmp) {
  467|       |            auto x = reinterpret_cast<T***>(tmp);
  468|       |            tmp = *x;
  469|       |            numAllocs *= 2;
  470|       |        }
  471|       |
  472|       |        return numAllocs;
  473|       |    }
  474|       |
  475|       |    // WARNING: Underflow if numBytes < ALIGNMENT! This is guarded in addOrFree().
  476|       |    void add(void* ptr, const size_t numBytes) noexcept {
  477|       |        const size_t numElements = (numBytes - ALIGNMENT) / ALIGNED_SIZE;
  478|       |
  479|       |        auto data = reinterpret_cast<T**>(ptr);
  480|       |
  481|       |        // link free list
  482|       |        auto x = reinterpret_cast<T***>(data);
  483|       |        *x = mListForFree;
  484|       |        mListForFree = data;
  485|       |
  486|       |        // create linked list for newly allocated data
  487|       |        auto* const headT =
  488|       |            reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<T*>(reinterpret_cast<char*>(ptr) + ALIGNMENT);
  489|       |
  490|       |        auto* const head = reinterpret_cast<char*>(headT);
  491|       |
  492|       |        // Visual Studio compiler automatically unrolls this loop, which is pretty cool
  493|       |        for (size_t i = 0; i < numElements; ++i) {
  494|       |            *reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<char**>(head + i * ALIGNED_SIZE) =
  495|       |                head + (i + 1) * ALIGNED_SIZE;
  496|       |        }
  497|       |
  498|       |        // last one points to 0
  499|       |        *reinterpret_cast_no_cast_align_warning<T**>(head + (numElements - 1) * ALIGNED_SIZE) =
  500|       |            mHead;
  501|       |        mHead = headT;
  502|       |    }
  503|       |
  504|       |    // Called when no memory is available (mHead == 0).
  505|       |    // Don't inline this slow path.
  506|       |    ROBIN_HOOD(NOINLINE) T* performAllocation() {
  507|       |        size_t const numElementsToAlloc = calcNumElementsToAlloc();
  508|       |
  509|       |        // alloc new memory: [prev |T, T, ... T]
  510|       |        size_t const bytes = ALIGNMENT + ALIGNED_SIZE * numElementsToAlloc;
  511|       |        ROBIN_HOOD_LOG("std::malloc " << bytes << " = " << ALIGNMENT << " + " << ALIGNED_SIZE
  512|       |                                      << " * " << numElementsToAlloc)
  513|       |        add(assertNotNull<std::bad_alloc>(std::malloc(bytes)), bytes);
  514|       |        return mHead;
  515|       |    }
  516|       |
  517|       |    // enforce byte alignment of the T's
  518|       |#if ROBIN_HOOD(CXX) >= ROBIN_HOOD(CXX14)
  519|       |    static constexpr size_t ALIGNMENT =
  520|       |        (std::max)(std::alignment_of<T>::value, std::alignment_of<T*>::value);
  521|       |#else
  522|       |    static const size_t ALIGNMENT =
  523|       |        (ROBIN_HOOD_STD::alignment_of<T>::value > ROBIN_HOOD_STD::alignment_of<T*>::value)
  524|       |            ? ROBIN_HOOD_STD::alignment_of<T>::value
  525|       |            : +ROBIN_HOOD_STD::alignment_of<T*>::value; // the + is for walkarround
  526|       |#endif
  527|       |
  528|       |    static constexpr size_t ALIGNED_SIZE = ((sizeof(T) - 1) / ALIGNMENT + 1) * ALIGNMENT;
  529|       |
  530|       |    static_assert(MinNumAllocs >= 1, "MinNumAllocs");
  531|       |    static_assert(MaxNumAllocs >= MinNumAllocs, "MaxNumAllocs");
  532|       |    static_assert(ALIGNED_SIZE >= sizeof(T*), "ALIGNED_SIZE");
  533|       |    static_assert(0 == (ALIGNED_SIZE % sizeof(T*)), "ALIGNED_SIZE mod");
  534|       |    static_assert(ALIGNMENT >= sizeof(T*), "ALIGNMENT");
  535|       |
  536|       |    T* mHead{nullptr};
  537|       |    T** mListForFree{nullptr};
  538|       |};

  865|       |// using wrapper classes for hash and key_equal prevents the diamond problem when the same type
  866|       |// is used. see https://stackoverflow.com/a/28771920/48181
  867|       |template <typename T>
  868|       |struct WrapHash : public T {
  869|       |    WrapHash() = default;
  870|       |    explicit WrapHash(T const& o) noexcept(noexcept(T(std::declval<T const&>())))
  871|       |        : T(o) {}
  872|       |};
  873|       |
  874|       |template <typename T>
  875|       |struct WrapKeyEqual : public T {
  876|       |    WrapKeyEqual() = default;
  877|       |    explicit WrapKeyEqual(T const& o) noexcept(noexcept(T(std::declval<T const&>())))
  878|       |        : T(o) {}
  879|       |};
  880|       |
  881|       |// A highly optimized hashmap implementation, using the Robin Hood algorithm.
  882|       |//
  883|       |// In most cases, this map should be usable as a drop-in replacement for std::unordered_map, but
  884|       |// be about 2x faster in most cases and require much less allocations.
  885|       |//
  886|       |// This implementation uses the following memory layout:
  887|       |//
  888|       |// [Node, Node, ... Node | info, info, ... infoSentinel ]
  889|       |//
  890|       |// * Node: either a DataNode that directly has the std::pair<key, val> as member,
  891|       |//   or a DataNode with a pointer to std::pair<key,val>. Which DataNode representation to use
  892|       |//   depends on how fast the swap() operation is. Heuristically, this is automatically choosen
  893|       |//   based on sizeof(). there are always 2^n Nodes.
  894|       |//
  895|       |// * info: Each Node in the map has a corresponding info byte, so there are 2^n info bytes.
  896|       |//   Each byte is initialized to 0, meaning the corresponding Node is empty. Set to 1 means the
  897|       |//   corresponding node contains data. Set to 2 means the corresponding Node is filled, but it
  898|       |//   actually belongs to the previous position and was pushed out because that place is already
  899|       |//   taken.
  900|       |//
  901|       |// * infoSentinel: Sentinel byte set to 1, so that iterator's ++ can stop at end() without the
  902|       |//   need for a idx variable.
  903|       |//
  904|       |// According to STL, order of templates has effect on throughput. That's why I've moved the
  905|       |// boolean to the front.
  906|       |// https://www.reddit.com/r/cpp/comments/ahp6iu/compile_time_binary_size_reductions_and_cs_future/eeguck4/
  907|       |template <bool IsFlat, size_t MaxLoadFactor100, typename Key, typename T, typename Hash,
  908|       |          typename KeyEqual>
  909|       |class Table
  910|       |    : public WrapHash<Hash>,
  911|       |      public WrapKeyEqual<KeyEqual>,
  912|       |      detail::NodeAllocator<
  913|       |          typename std::conditional<
  914|       |              std::is_void<T>::value, Key,
  915|       |              robin_hood::pair<typename std::conditional<IsFlat, Key, Key const>::type, T>>::type,
  916|       |          4, 16384, IsFlat> {
  917|       |public:
  918|       |    static constexpr bool is_flat = IsFlat;
  919|       |    static constexpr bool is_map = !std::is_void<T>::value;
  920|       |    static constexpr bool is_set = !is_map;
  921|       |    static constexpr bool is_transparent =
  922|       |        has_is_transparent<Hash>::value && has_is_transparent<KeyEqual>::value;
  923|       |
  924|       |    using key_type = Key;
  925|       |    using mapped_type = T;
  926|       |    using value_type = typename std::conditional<
  927|       |        is_set, Key,
  928|       |        robin_hood::pair<typename std::conditional<is_flat, Key, Key const>::type, T>>::type;
  929|       |    using size_type = size_t;
  930|       |    using hasher = Hash;
  931|       |    using key_equal = KeyEqual;
  932|       |    using Self = Table<IsFlat, MaxLoadFactor100, key_type, mapped_type, hasher, key_equal>;
  933|       |
  934|       |private:
  935|       |    static_assert(MaxLoadFactor100 > 10 && MaxLoadFactor100 < 100,
  936|       |                  "MaxLoadFactor100 needs to be >10 && < 100");
  937|       |
  938|       |    using WHash = WrapHash<Hash>;
  939|       |    using WKeyEqual = WrapKeyEqual<KeyEqual>;
  940|       |
  941|       |    // configuration defaults
  942|       |
  943|       |    // make sure we have 8 elements, needed to quickly rehash mInfo
  944|       |    static constexpr size_t InitialNumElements = sizeof(uint64_t);
  945|       |    static constexpr uint32_t InitialInfoNumBits = 5;
  946|       |    static constexpr uint8_t InitialInfoInc = 1U << InitialInfoNumBits;
  947|       |    static constexpr size_t InfoMask = InitialInfoInc - 1U;
  948|       |    static constexpr uint8_t InitialInfoHashShift = 0;
  949|       |    using DataPool = detail::NodeAllocator<value_type, 4, 16384, IsFlat>;
  950|       |
  951|       |    // type needs to be wider than uint8_t.
  952|       |    using InfoType = uint32_t;

 1146|       |
 1147|       |    // fast path: Just copy data, without allocating anything.
 1148|       |    template <typename M>
 1149|       |    struct Cloner<M, true> {
 1150|       |        void operator()(M const& source, M& target) const {
 1151|       |            auto const* const src = reinterpret_cast<char const*>(source.mKeyVals);
 1152|       |            auto* tgt = reinterpret_cast<char*>(target.mKeyVals);
 1153|       |            auto const numElementsWithBuffer = target.calcNumElementsWithBuffer(target.mMask + 1);
 1154|       |            std::copy(src, src + target.calcNumBytesTotal(numElementsWithBuffer), tgt);
 1155|       |        }
 1156|       |    };
 1157|       |
 1158|       |    template <typename M>
 1159|       |    struct Cloner<M, false> {
 1160|       |        void operator()(M const& s, M& t) const {
 1161|       |            auto const numElementsWithBuffer = t.calcNumElementsWithBuffer(t.mMask + 1);
 1162|       |            std::copy(s.mInfo, s.mInfo + t.calcNumBytesInfo(numElementsWithBuffer), t.mInfo);
 1163|       |
 1164|       |            for (size_t i = 0; i < numElementsWithBuffer; ++i) {
 1165|       |                if (t.mInfo[i]) {
 1166|       |                    ::new (static_cast<void*>(t.mKeyVals + i)) Node(t, *s.mKeyVals[i]);
 1167|       |                }
 1168|       |            }
 1169|       |        }
 1170|       |    };

 1222|       |    // generic iterator for both const_iterator and iterator.
 1223|       |    template <bool IsConst>
 1224|       |    // NOLINTNEXTLINE(hicpp-special-member-functions,cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions)
 1225|       |    class Iter {
 1226|       |    private:
 1227|       |        using NodePtr = typename std::conditional<IsConst, Node const*, Node*>::type;
 1228|       |
 1229|       |    public:
 1230|       |        using difference_type = std::ptrdiff_t;
 1231|       |        using value_type = typename Self::value_type;
 1232|       |        using reference = typename std::conditional<IsConst, value_type const&, value_type&>::type;
 1233|       |        using pointer = typename std::conditional<IsConst, value_type const*, value_type*>::type;
 1234|       |        using iterator_category = std::forward_iterator_tag;
 1235|       |
 1236|       |        // default constructed iterator can be compared to itself, but WON'T return true when
 1237|       |        // compared to end().
 1238|       |        Iter() = default;
 1239|       |
 1240|       |        // Rule of zero: nothing specified. The conversion constructor is only enabled for
 1241|       |        // iterator to const_iterator, so it doesn't accidentally work as a copy ctor.
 1242|       |
 1243|       |        // Conversion constructor from iterator to const_iterator.
 1244|       |        template <bool OtherIsConst,
 1245|       |                  typename = typename std::enable_if<IsConst && !OtherIsConst>::type>
 1246|       |        // NOLINTNEXTLINE(hicpp-explicit-conversions)
 1247|       |        Iter(Iter<OtherIsConst> const& other) noexcept
 1248|       |            : mKeyVals(other.mKeyVals)
 1249|       |            , mInfo(other.mInfo) {}
 1250|       |
 1251|       |        Iter(NodePtr valPtr, uint8_t const* infoPtr) noexcept
 1252|      0|            : mKeyVals(valPtr)
 1253|      0|            , mInfo(infoPtr) {}
 1254|       |
 1255|       |        Iter(NodePtr valPtr, uint8_t const* infoPtr,
 1256|       |             fast_forward_tag ROBIN_HOOD_UNUSED(tag) /*unused*/) noexcept
 1257|       |            : mKeyVals(valPtr)
 1258|       |            , mInfo(infoPtr) {
 1259|       |            fastForward();
 1260|       |        }
 1261|       |
 1262|       |        template <bool OtherIsConst,
 1263|       |                  typename = typename std::enable_if<IsConst && !OtherIsConst>::type>
 1264|       |        Iter& operator=(Iter<OtherIsConst> const& other) noexcept {
 1265|       |            mKeyVals = other.mKeyVals;
 1266|       |            mInfo = other.mInfo;
 1267|       |            return *this;
 1268|       |        }
 1269|       |
 1270|       |        // prefix increment. Undefined behavior if we are at end()!
 1271|       |        Iter& operator++() noexcept {
 1272|       |            mInfo++;
 1273|       |            mKeyVals++;
 1274|       |            fastForward();
 1275|       |            return *this;
 1276|       |        }
 1277|       |
 1278|       |        Iter operator++(int) noexcept {
 1279|       |            Iter tmp = *this;
 1280|       |            ++(*this);
 1281|       |            return tmp;
 1282|       |        }
 1283|       |
 1284|       |        reference operator*() const {
 1285|       |            return **mKeyVals;
 1286|       |        }
 1287|       |
 1288|      0|        pointer operator->() const {
 1289|      0|            return &**mKeyVals;
 1290|      0|        }
 1291|       |
 1292|       |        template <bool O>
 1293|      0|        bool operator==(Iter<O> const& o) const noexcept {
 1294|      0|            return mKeyVals == o.mKeyVals;
 1295|      0|        }
 1296|       |
 1297|       |        template <bool O>
 1298|       |        bool operator!=(Iter<O> const& o) const noexcept {
 1299|       |            return mKeyVals != o.mKeyVals;
 1300|       |        }
 1301|       |
 1302|       |    private:
 1303|       |        // fast forward to the next non-free info byte
 1304|       |        // I've tried a few variants that don't depend on intrinsics, but unfortunately they are
 1305|       |        // quite a bit slower than this one. So I've reverted that change again. See map_benchmark.
 1306|       |        void fastForward() noexcept {
 1307|       |            size_t n = 0;
 1308|       |            while (0U == (n = detail::unaligned_load<size_t>(mInfo))) {
 1309|       |                mInfo += sizeof(size_t);
 1310|       |                mKeyVals += sizeof(size_t);
 1311|       |            }
 1312|       |#if defined(ROBIN_HOOD_DISABLE_INTRINSICS)
 1313|       |            // we know for certain that within the next 8 bytes we'll find a non-zero one.
 1314|       |            if (ROBIN_HOOD_UNLIKELY(0U == detail::unaligned_load<uint32_t>(mInfo))) {
 1315|       |                mInfo += 4;
 1316|       |                mKeyVals += 4;
 1317|       |            }
 1318|       |            if (ROBIN_HOOD_UNLIKELY(0U == detail::unaligned_load<uint16_t>(mInfo))) {
 1319|       |                mInfo += 2;
 1320|       |                mKeyVals += 2;
 1321|       |            }
 1322|       |            if (ROBIN_HOOD_UNLIKELY(0U == *mInfo)) {
 1323|       |                mInfo += 1;
 1324|       |                mKeyVals += 1;
 1325|       |            }
 1326|       |#else
 1327|       |#    if ROBIN_HOOD(LITTLE_ENDIAN)
 1328|       |            auto inc = ROBIN_HOOD_COUNT_TRAILING_ZEROES(n) / 8;
 1329|       |#    else
 1330|       |            auto inc = ROBIN_HOOD_COUNT_LEADING_ZEROES(n) / 8;
 1331|       |#    endif
 1332|       |            mInfo += inc;
 1333|       |            mKeyVals += inc;
 1334|       |#endif
 1335|       |        }
 1336|       |
 1337|       |        friend class Table<IsFlat, MaxLoadFactor100, key_type, mapped_type, hasher, key_equal>;
 1338|       |        NodePtr mKeyVals{nullptr};
 1339|       |        uint8_t const* mInfo{nullptr};
 1340|       |    };

 1342|       |    ////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 1343|       |

 2343|       |    // Finds key, and if not already present prepares a spot where to pot the key & value.
 2344|       |    // This potentially shifts nodes out of the way, updates mInfo and number of inserted
 2345|       |    // elements, so the only operation left to do is create/assign a new node at that spot.

 2347|      0|    std::pair<size_t, InsertionState> insertKeyPrepareEmptySpot(OtherKey&& key) {
 2348|      0|        for (int i = 0; i < 256; ++i) {

 1204|       |    {
 1205|       |        return const_reverse_iterator( cbegin() );
